case_summary.text: GST : Where applicant has been awarded a contract by Airport Authority of India for construction of residential colony for staff and employees, construction of residential colony by applicant attracts GST at rate of 12 per cent as per entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017
12% GST on construction of residential colony for staff and employees of Airport Authority of India : AAR

GST : Where applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), activity undertaken by applicant is supply of works contract service to a Govt. entity covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST

GST : Where construction of residential quarters for employees of power plant are exclusively meant for use of employees of NPCIL, a government entity, and aforesaid construction is ancillary to attainment of main object of NPCIL, therefore applicant-assessee is eligible for concessional rate of 12% under Entry 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T.(Rate) dated 28.06.2017 for period up to 31.12.2021.

GST : Where applicant is awarded a contract with Railways for repair work, addition and alteration of existing structure, services of repair, maintenance, renovation of residential complex meant for use of railway employees are covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and are taxable at 12 per cent GST

GST : Where applicant who is promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing residential housing project 'Akriti', works contract service received from contractors for construction of those dwelling units that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of said notification, provided applicant does not opt for paying tax at rate specified in Entry No. 3(ie) Entry No. 3(if)

GST : Where applicant is engaged in development of residential project called 'SAMANVAY RESIDENCY', which falls under affordable housing project, construction services provided by applicant qualifies for reduced tax rate of 12 per cent GST as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Where applicant constructed residential units on land belonging to flood victims under a rehabilitation project awarded to it by a charitable trust, activity squarely falls within scope of works contract under section 2(119) and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Where applicant is engaged in business of construction and development of residential and commercial complex, since project undertaken by it falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing', applicant's case is covered under tax rate of 12 per cent under Heading No. 9954 (Construction Services), mentioned in Notification No. 11/2017-CT-(Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Where applicant was providing works contract services to National Centre for Biological Science(NCBS), since NCBS was neither a Government authority or a Government entity nor this institute was established to carry out a function entrusted by Government, services provided by applicant to NCBS was taxable at rate of 9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent KGST under residential item no. (xii) of Serial no. 3 of Notification no. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28.6.2017 as amended from time to tim

GST : Where applicant enters into contract with a company for construction of residential complex, its case would be covered under concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since project undertaken by them falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing'. However,

GST : Where applicant is engaged in promotion of gated community villas for prospective villa buyers and it buys land and divides same into plots and sells plots to villa buyers and while booking of plots happens it enters into construction agreement with villa buyers to construct and transfer villa to villa buyers on payment of agreed consideration as per agreed conditions in construction agreement, applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 1.5 per cent in respect of services of construction of affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (i) and at rate of 7.5 per cent in respect of services of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 subject to conditions prescribed under respective entries in villa projects

GST : Where ongoing residential project did not fall under affordable housing scheme, services of construction of all types of residential apartments in said ongoing housing project during period from 1-7-2017 to 31-3-2019 do not qualify for concessional rate of 12 per cent and is liable to GST at rate of 18 per cent as per item (i) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : If projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, construction service provided by applicant to developer under residential project is liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent KGST as provided in Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; else,

GST : Composite supply of works contract that includes construction of school building, school and college hostel, staff quarters, etc provided to State Government is subject to 12% GST as it is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : If projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, construction service provided by applicant to developer under residential project is liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent KGST as provided in Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; else, services will be liable to tax at rate of 9 per cent under CGST Act and at rate of 9 per cent under KGST Act as provided in Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Composite supply of works contract that includes construction of school building, school and college hostel, staff quarters, etc. provided to State Government is subject to 12% GST as it is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for Karnataka Slum Development Board under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana as a main contractor is liable to 12% GST (6% CGST + 6% SGST) till 17-7-2022 in terms of Sl. No. 3(iv)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended and thereafter, such services are liable to 18% GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of said Notification. However, these services when provided by sub-contractor are also liable to 18% GST.

CGST : Where project 'Prajapati Magnum' undertaken by applicants falls under definition of "Affordable Housing", applicant's case is covered under tax rate of 12% under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v) (da) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, but benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018 i.e. date on which Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and benefit of this reduced rate would be

GST : GST on construction of unit which is other than affordable residential apartments by applicant in Residential Real Estate Project(RREP) promoted by them, namely, Ashiana Shubham-Phase IV in Chennai is classifiable under SAC 9954 as 'Construction Service' and applicable rate of tax is CGST at rate of 3.75 per cent and SGST at rate of 3.75 per cent as per Entry Sl. No. 3(ia) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended

GST : Works contract service of construction provided by appellant to IIT Bhubaneshwar is eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent in terms of entry at S. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (R)
12% GST on construction of residential quarters exclusively meant for use of employees of NPCIL up to 31.12.2021: AAAR

GST : Activity of composite supply of works contract service by way of construction of fish market for Panchayat (Road and Building) Division, Valsad District Panchayat merits classification at Serial Number 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is eligible for 12 per cent GST

GST : Where applicant is awarded contract for providing services in relation to maintenance of various colonies developed by Chhattisgarh Housing Board which involves supply of goods and services, as three conditions to qualify for benefit of Nil rate of GST as provided under Sl. No. 3/3A to Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended are not satisfied, exemption is not available
GST : Exemption provided in Sl. No. 12 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 will be applicable to applicant providing residential dwellings owned by it for use as residence

GST : Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under 'residual item' under item No. (xii) of Serial No.3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6- 2017

GST : Construction and commission of jetty/berth by applicant port trust 'COPT' for Indian Coast Guard (ICG) is supply of 'works contract'; as consideration for services received by COPT is grants from Central Government, condition in Sl. No. 9C of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) is not satisfied and COPT is not eligible for exemption; as services are provided to Central Government for ICG's activities as public authority, applicant will be eligible to concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent under entry at Item (vi) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) for services supplied between 21-9-2017 and 17-7-2022

GST : Where applicant sub-contracts for construction of independent houses under main contract of construction of houses pertaining to Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana is covered under sub-item (c) of item (iv) of serial number 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 is liable to CGST at 6 per cent and similarly same is also liable to KGST at 6 per cent under Karnataka Goods and Services Act, 2017

GST : Applicant-real estate developer having exercised its option for continuing with payment of tax at old rates in respect to its ongoing project of construction of residential apartments should pay GST at rate of 18 per cent; since project is not covered under any of schemes specified under Item (ie) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), applicant is not eligible for concessional rate of tax of 12 per cent

GST : Where applicant owner of land enter into a joint development agreement with developer for development of residential apartments in which cost of construction shall be borne by Developer and applicant would get 32 per cent share of apartments, applicant is liable to pay tax as per entries 3(i) to 3(id) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 depending on nature of apartment

GST : Works contract services performed by assessee as per contracts awarded by Kerela State film development corporation Ltd, a government authority to construct a cultural complex is in nature of construction of structure meant predominantly for use as a cultural establishment and is liable to GST at 12 per cent as per Sl 3(vi)(b) of Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : Where applicant is engaged in construction of residential complex in two parts i.e. Part-A and Part-B, in view of fact that 50 per cent or more of FAR/FSI of entire housing project comprising of Part-A and Part-B has not been used for construction of dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 sq. meters., applicant is not eligible for benefit of reduced rate of tax as provided under Entry3(v)(da) of Notification No.11/2017 CT( Rate) dated 28-06-2017 as amended by Notification No.01/2018 CT(Rate) dated 25-01-2018

GST: Where applicant (Government Entity) proposes to transfer by way of lease vacant plots of Maharashtra State Government to Panvel Municipal Corporation (PMC) for use as PMC Commissioner's residence and PMC Mayor's residence, supply of services by applicant of transfer by way of lease of vacant plots will be taxable at rate of 18 per cent under Sl. No. 16, clause (iii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Where applicant has been awarded a contract by NBCC for construction of ISPAT Post Graduate Medical Institute and Super Speciality Hospital for SAIL in Odisha on Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) basis, instant supply is a 'Composite Supply of works contract service' provided in relation to construction of civil structure meant pre-dominantly for use as a clinical establishment; since supply is being made to NBCC which is a body corporate and not to any Government or Government entity, pre-requisite to merit classification under SI. No. 3(vi)(a) or (b) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is not fulfilled; since composite supply of works contract services have been entrusted by Central Government, supply of works contract service would merit entitlement for concessional rate of GST at rate of 12 per cent [CGST at rate of 6 per cent + SGST at rate of 6 per cent] in terms of SI. No. 3(ix) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Villas being constructed and sold by applicant are "residential apartment", projects are "real estate project" and applicant is "promoter"; services of applicant are construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item No. (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate) and liable to GST @ 7.5% [3.75% - CGST + 3.75% - SGST];

GST : Where petitioner, a joint venture formed for executing railway projects, was assigned a works contract by RVNL for various railway infrastructure developments and it paid GST at 12% under Serial No.3(v)(a) of Notification No.11/2017, but was later issued a demand for an 18% tax rate by revenue, expression "pertaining to" in said notification has a wide import,

GST : Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam not being a local authority in terms of section 2(69)(c) of CGST Act, 2017 but a Governmental authority as defined under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), services of construction of non-commercial establishments rendered to its Construction and Design Services Division are liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) instead of 12 per cent in terms Sl. No. 3(iii) of said Notification as amended with effect from 1-1-2022

GST : Villas being constructed by applicant are "residential apartment", projects are "real estate project" and applicant is "promoter"; services of applicant are construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item No. (ia) of SI. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 ibid and liable to GST @ 7.5% deduction of one-third of total amount charged for supply in arriving at taxable value of supply,

GST : Works contract services performed by assessee as per contracts awarded by M/s Kerela State film development corporation Ltd, a government authority to construct a cultural complex is in nature of construction of structure meant for predominantly use as a cultural establishment and is liable to GST at 12 percent as per Sl 3(vi)(b)of Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : Where applicant launched an Affordable Housing Project (Affordable Group Housing Colony) in Gurugram under scheme approved by Government of Haryana (Affordable Housing Policy, 2013) and started construction of flats over land before 31-3-2019, project over said land is an ongoing project as construction was started before 31-3-2019 and, therefore, rate of tax applicable in respect of flats is 12 per cent (with input tax + land abatement) in view of Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 as applicant submitted an option to pay GST at old effective rate of 8 per cent and 12 per cent with input tax credit

GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

GST : Works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for Airport Authorities of India performed by applicant being used in process of commerce and business is appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent

GST : Since applicant-assessee is not satisfying any of three mandatory conditions specified in Sl. No. 3/3A of exemption Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended for exemption, therefore, services provided by applicant in relation to maintenance of various colonies developed by Chhattisgarh Housing Board (CGHB) and not handed over to local authority by CGHB,

No. 3(vi)(a) or 3(vi)(b) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended

GST : Where constructed villas are 'residential apartment' other than 'affordable residential apartments' and projects are 'real estate project', builder of villas is 'promoter'; services provided by builder are residential apartments construction other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item No. (ia) of Sl. HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) - Whether since control over BDA rests with Govt. of Karnataka, BDA is a Government entity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant involves supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and, hence, is a 'works contract' within meaning of section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether transaction of applicant would be a supply of works contract services covered under clause (a) of Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 10.8, 10.9.2  11]GST : Where applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), activity undertaken by applicant is supply of works contract service to a Govt. entity covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST

FACT: The applicant is engaged in the business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services. The applicant has applied for the civil construction work tender with Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) with respect to construction of residential complexes/row of residential houses.

The said project is allotted to the applicant and the same has been executed by the Company through appointing various contractors.

The applicant has sought advance ruling in respect of the question as to whether the activity undertaken by the applicant is covered under section 2(119); whether Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Authority as per the provisions of GST Law and the rate of tax applicable to the transaction of the applicant and more so whether the transactions are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended).

According to applicant, its activity of construction of residential house and residential complex with respect to following BDA projects (to Government Authority) are squarely covered under the definition of Works Contract and their activity will be considered as supply of services.

The applicant submits that as per the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), the activity undertaken by the applicant to BDA i.e., Government Authority is liable for GST at 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST.

HELD: For a works contract to be covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 the following conditions needs to be satisfied:

(a)

The recipient of services must be a Government Entity and in this case, Bangalore Development Authority;

(b)

FACT: The Applicant is a Private Limited Company engaged in the business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services. It has sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

(a)

Whether the activity undertaken by the applicant is covered under section 2(119) of the CGST Act, 2017?

(b)

Whether Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Authority as per the provisions of GST Law?

(c)

Whether the transaction covered under point 3(ii) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended?

(d)

Whether the transaction covered under point 3(ix) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended?

HELD: The transaction of the applicant is verified where in applicant got work orders from the Principal contractor for the construction of 2 and 3 BHK Housing projects on behalf of Bangalore Development Authority.

Further on verification of the records it is observed that Bengaluru Development Authority has issued work orders to main contractor Gowri Infra Engineers Private Limited (GIEPL) to construct 2 and 3-BHK Housing Project on lump sum turnkey basis based on Tender's Own design under Two cover System. [Para 11.3]

The main issue is the rate of tax applicable to the transaction of the applicant and more so whether the transactions are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended). The applicant himself has clearly stated that his transactions are not covered under entry No. 3(ii) of the said notification and hence they are not considered as the same is also agreed by this Authority. [Para 11.4]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Civil construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant-company is engaged in business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor - It seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether construction services proposed to be provided by applicant will qualify for reduced GST rate of 12 per cent as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Low cost houses in an affordable housing project having area of 60 sq. mts. or upto 60 sq. mts. will attract 12 per cent GST - Whether since project undertaken by applicant is an affordable housing project, it will attract rate of 12 per cent GST under Sr. No. 3 of said Notification – Held, yes [Para 5.8][In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant undertook project of construction of residential flat (Low cost flats) having carpet area of upto or less than 60 sq. mts. and its project falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing Project', applicant's case is covered under concessional tax rate slab of 12 per cent

FACT: The applicant-company is engaged in the business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor. It had filed the instant application in respect of a proposed civil construction contract to be entered into with a developer for construction of a residential project comprising of 135 buildings all having residential flats/units having carpet area of up to or less than 60 Sq. Mts. According to them, since more than 50 per cent of PSI is utilized towards construction of LCH, the project would qualify as an 'Affordable Housing Project' (AHP).

It seeks advance ruling on the issue as to whether the construction services proposed to be provided by the applicant will qualify for the reduced CGST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST), as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

HELD: As per Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) dated 25-1-2018, low-cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house in an affordable housing project which has been given infrastructure status vide notification of Government of India, in Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs vide F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated the 30-3-2017 will attract tax rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST.) [Para 5.3]

This clause will be applicable to the applicant if the project undertaken by them is an affordable housing project which has been given infrastructure status vide Government of India notification mentioned above. [Para 5.4]

Department of Economic Affairs' notification issued vide F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated the 30th March,2017 has included Affordable Housing under the column 'Infrastructure sub-sector' against the category of Social and Commercial Infrastructure. [Para 5.5]

One of the recommendations made by the GST Council in its 25th meeting held on 18-1-2018 at Delhi was to extend the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sq. mts. in a housing project which has been given infrastructure status under Notification No.13/06/2009 dated 30-3-2009. The said notification of Department of Economic Affairs provides infrastructure status to Affordable Housing. The recommendation of the Council would extend the concessional rate to construction of flats/houses of less than 60 sq. mts. in projects other than the projects covered by any scheme of the Central or State Government also. FACT: The applicant is the promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing a residential housing project named 'Akriti' (RREP).

The applicant wants to know whether Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (Rate Notification), as amended time-to-time, applies to the works contract service received from the contractors.

HELD: Entry No. 3(v)(da) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is related to the construction of low-cost apartments. Clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of the Rate Notification defines an affordable residential apartment. It shall mean a residential apartment in a project which commences on or after 1-4-2019 or in an ongoing project in respect of which the promoter has not exercised the option to pay tax at the rate specified in (ie) or (if) of Entry No. 3, having carpet area not exceeding 60 sq. mtr. in metropolitan cities or 90 sq. mtr. In cities or towns other than metropolitan cities and for which the gross amount charged is not more than 45 lakhs. [Para 4.1]

The flats having a carpet area of 60 sq. mtr. or less per unit in the RREP qualify as affordable residential apartments, provided the gross amount charged per unit does not exceed Rs. 45 lakhs and the promoter has not exercised the option to pay tax at the rate specified in (ie) or (if) of Entry No. 3. It now needs to be ascertained whether the RREP is an affordable housing project, which enjoys infrastructure status vide the AHP Notification. [Para 4.6]

Affordable housing has been defined in the AHP Notification as a housing project using at least 50 per cent of FAR/FSI for dwelling units with a carpet area of not more than 60 sq. mtr. The term 'carpet area' has been assigned the same meaning as in section 2(k) of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. It means the net usable floor area of an apartment, excluding the area covered by the external walls, areas under services shafts, balcony or veranda and open terrace, but includes the area covered by the internal partition walls of the apartment. [Para 4.7]

The Floor Area Ratio (FAR), also known as the Floor Space Ratio (FSR) or the Floor Space Index (FSI), depicts the relationship between the total usable floor space in a building and the total area of the plot on which the building is constructed. In mathematical terms, FAR = CA/LA, where CA = Constructed area or built-up area, and LA = Land area. [Para 4.8]

Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in Column 3 of the Table in the said Notification, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein. One of the recommendations made by the GST Council in its 25th meeting held on 18-1-2018 at Delhi was to extend the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sq. m. in a housing project which has been given infrastructure status under Notification No. 13/06/2009, dated 30-3-2009. The said notification of Department of Economic Affairs provides infrastructure status to Affordable Housing. The recommendation of the Council would extend the concessional rate to construction of flats/houses of less than 60 sq. m. in projects other than the projects covered by any scheme of the Central or State Government also. The GST Council has also observed that it may be recalled that all inputs used in and capital goods deployed for construction of flats, houses, etc. attract GST of 18 per cent or 28 per cent. As against this, most of the housing projects in the affordable segment in the country would now attract GST of 8 per cent (after deducting value of land). As a result, the builder or developer will not be required to pay GST on the construction service of flats etc. in cash but would have enough ITC (input tax credits) in his books to pay the output GST, in which case, he should not recover any GST payable on the flats from the buyers. He can recover GST from the buyers of flats only if he recalibrates the cost of flat after factoring in the full ITC available in the GST regime and reduces the ex-GST price of flats. The GST Council has also mentioned that the builders/developers are expected to follow the principles laid down under section 171 of the GST Act (Anti-Profiteering Rules) scrupulously.

In response to a request for clarification to enable availing 8 per cent GST on Affordable Housing made by the builders association namely, CREDAI vide their letter No. CREDAI/MoF/2018/14, dated 19-3-2018, the Government vide F. No. 354/52/2018-TRU, Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue (TRU), dated 7-5-2018 has clarified that 'Low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house in an affordable housing project, which has been given infrastructure status under notification F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated the 30-3-2017 of MOF (DEA), attract concessional GST of 8 per cent (the value of the undivided share of land is included in the price of the house). Whether the housing project qualifies as affordable housing project or not, shall be determined by the builder/developer as per the definition of affordable housing given in the abovementioned notification (i.e., affordable housing has been defined as a housing project using at least 50 per cent of FAR/FSI for dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 SQM). No certificate from any authority is required.'

From a reading of the above clarification, notification and the clause (da) of item (v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and facts on record, it is found that the applicant's case is covered under the tax rate of 12 per cent, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing' as stated by them in the application. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in the cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018, i.e., the date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable in case of only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. In this scheme which is covered in the category of affordable housing. In case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. the applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate. [Para 5]

Thus, the construction services provided by the applicant under the project "Prajapati Magnum" qualifies for the reduced CGST rate of 6% as provided in Sr. No. 3-item (v)-sub item (da) of Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018. [Para 6]

MPPGCL has been established by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in the company and is also exercising full control over the activities of the said company. Thus, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST law, as it fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions laid down under notification No. 11/2017. [Para 5.4] Now, the said Government Entity i.e. MPPGCL has been entrusted with the work of power generation in the State of Madhya Pradesh. The essential and sole work entrusted to MPPGCL by the Government of Madhya Pradesh is of electricity (power) generation. MPPGCL has awarded a works contract for construction of 599 residential quarters to the applicant. However, the civil construction of residential quarters is neither the primary work entrusted to MPPGCL nor it has any bearing on the work i.e. power generation by any means. Thus, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent GST should not be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant. The intention of the legislature has been to give concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general. Any work having direct involvement in the entrusted work i.e. power generation would merit exemption envisaged under Sr.No.3(vi)(c) of the Notification No.11/2017-CT (Rate) under CGST Act and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of MPPGCL will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. [Para 5.5]

The activity in question definitely did not have any relation to the principal work of power generation entrusted by the State Government to MPPGCL, and, thus, the works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No.11/2017-CT Rate dated 28-6-2017 and corresponding notification under MPGST Act, 2017. [Para 5.6]

Thus, the impugned activity of the applicant would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) classifiable under SAC 9954 read with Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017. [Para 5.7]

The Floor Area Ratio (FAR), also known as the Floor Space Ratio (FSR) or the Floor Space Index (FSI), depicts the relationship between the total usable floor space in a building and the total area of the plot on which the building is constructed. In mathematical terms, FAR = CA/LA, where CA = Constructed area or built-up area, and LA = Land area. The built-up area for the affordable residential apartments, as identified by the architect, under the RREP is 7885 sq. mtr. (the calculation sheet is attached). The relevant FAR, therefore, comes out to be 1.401, which is 50.96 per cent of the FAR for the project. The RREP, therefore, is an affordable housing project in terms of the AHP Notification. Lease of plots to NMMC for Indoor Recreation Centre

The NMMC proposes to set up the Indoor Recreation Centre which shall consist of a gymnasium, swimming pool and play courts, all of which facilities shall be accessible to the general public for a nominal fee. This can be considered to be a kind of a Public Amenity which is given to the citizens of the country and the public at large. Sr. No. 17 of the Twelfth Schedule under article 243W of the Constitution is with respect to 'Public amenities including street lighting, parking lots, bus stops and public conveniences'. An Indoor Recreation Centre can be considered as a kind of amenity which is given to the public by the local authority for recreation and the same would be similar to amenities provided by the Municipalities in their jurisdiction. Hence plots are leased by the applicant (a kind of pure services) to a Municipality, i.e., a local authority in relation to a function entrusted to such Municipality under article 243W of the Constitution and would be exempt as per Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Lease of plots to NMMC for Slaughter House

Sr. No. 18 of the Twelfth Schedule under article 243W of the Constitution is with respect to 'Regulation of Slaughter Houses and Tanneries'. Hence plots leased by the applicant (a kind of pure services) to a Municipality, i.e., a local authority for setting up Slaughter Houses can be perceived to be in relation to a function entrusted to such Municipality under article 243W of the Constitution (Regulation of Slaughter Houses and Tanneries) and would be exempt as per Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Lease of plots to PMC for PMC Ward Office

PMC is a Municipal Corporation, a local authority. Article 243W of the Constitution of India has endowed Municipalities with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government with respect to — (i) the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice; (ii) the performance of functions and the implementation of schemes as may be entrusted to them including those in relation to the matters listed in the Twelfth Schedule, etc. To carry out such work it is imperative that PMC must have an office/s for its staff who are employed to perform the services of PMC. The jurisdiction of all Municipalities in India including PMC consists of Wards. Ward Offices are necessary for PMC to enable the execution or performance of all of its functions including those under article 243W of the Constitution. In the absence of the establishment by way of a Ward Office, PMC would find it impossible to function. The said services would be exempt as per Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The State jurisdiction officer has stated that this is the explanation given by Tax Research Unit (TRU) in F.No.332/04/2017, dated 5-9-2017. However, there is no such clarification in the above letter. Further, this is an incorrect way of reading the notification. [Para 7.2] The start of the Notification No. 12/2017-C.T.(Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended states that the Central government 'exempts the intra-State supply of services of description as specified in column (3) of the Table' from 'so much of the central tax' 'as is in excess of the said tax calculated at the rate as specified in the corresponding entry in column (4) of the said Table'. In respect to Sl No 77 (c) of this notification the description of the services is 'Service by an unincorporated body or a non- profit entity registered under any law for the time being in force, to its own members by way of reimbursement of charges or share of contribution up to an amount of 7500 rupees per month per member for sourcing of goods or services from a third person for the common use of its members in a housing society or a residential complex'. For these services the applicable central tax rate is nil as specified in column (4). Only services which exactly match this description are covered under this Sl No 77(c)of said Notification. In the instant case, this exemption is applicable only if the service by the applicant, a resident welfare association/housing society to its members by way of reimbursement of charges or share of contribution, for sourcing of goods or services from a third person for the common use of its members, is up to an amount of 7500 rupees per month per member. In the event the charges or share of contribution goes above 7500 rupees per month per member, such service will not fit the above description and hence, such service is not exempt. Such services are then fully chargeable to GST at the applicable tax rate. There is no option to the taxpayer to pick and choose from the description of the services mentioned in column (3) to make any service partly applicable to the notification and partly chargeable. Any service either falls within the scope of the description in column (3) or it does not. If a service by the applicant to its members by way of reimbursement of charges or share of contribution, for sourcing of goods or services from a third person for the common use of its members, is such that it is above 7500 rupees per month, it squarely falls outside the description of Sl No 77 (c) of Notification No. 12/2017-C.T.(Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended for CGST and of Sl.No. 77 (c) of Notification No. II(2)/CTR/532(d-15)/2017 vide G.O. (Ms) No. 73, dated 29-6-2017 as amended for SGST. GST at appropriate rates are to be charged on the full amount of reimbursement of charges or share of contribution. [Para 7.3]

In view of the above discussions, it is ruled that if a service by the applicant, a registered housing society/resident welfare association to its members by way of reimbursement of charges or share of contribution, for sourcing of goods or services from a third person for the common use of its members, is such that it is above 7500 rupees per month effective from 25-1-2018 (5000 rupees before), it is not eligible for exemption as per Sl.No. 77 (c) of Notification No.12/2017-C.T.(Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended for CGST and of Sl No 77 (c) of Notification No. II(2)/CTR/532(d-15)/2017 vide G.O. The applicant is undertaking a contract of works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for the Airport Authorities of India. The Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India has shown in the company profile that the shareholding of the Government of India in the Airport Authorities of India is 100 per cent and hence the AAI is a Government Entity.[Para 7.6] Further, the issue is whether the constructed works is a civil structure or any other original works. The runway and the apron etc. are structures which bear the load of the aircraft and provide a stable surface for the aircraft to operate. These are, therefore, civil structures. As per the AAI letters submitted by the applicant it is clear that the applicant is engaged in the extension of the runway and construction of new aprons and allied areas. Extension of the runway requires a new construction to be carried out and so does the apron and other areas. Therefore the applicant is engaged in construction of new civil structures. The term 'original works' is not defined in the Act, but the definition is provided in the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, to mean all new constructions;

(i)

all types of additions and alterations to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are required to make them workable;

(ii)

erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery or equipment or structures, whether pre-fabricated or otherwise.

The applicant is, therefore, engaged in construction of new civil structures. The activities carried out by the applicant are covered under the relevant serial number of the Notification. [Para 7.7]

The next issue is whether these works are meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession? In this regard, the original works done by the applicant are for use by the Airports Authority of India for supplying services to the Airway operations and hence is in the course of business. The airlines that use the runway and the aprons etc. constructed by the applicant work with a view to earn profits. They are engaged in commerce and business. Entry at Serial number 3(vi)(a) specifically provides that works be 'meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession'. As the works carried out by the applicant are used in the process of commerce and business, the applicant does not qualify for the works to be classified under Serial number 3(vi)(a). Hence the works contract performed by the applicant cannot be considered as covered under Serial No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 6 per cent, but are more appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of the of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent.[Para 7.8]

An explanation has been inserted to the above entry by Notification No. 17/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 26-7-2018, which provides that for the purposes of this item, the term 'business' shall not include any activity or transaction undertaken by the Central Government, a State Government or any local authority in which they are engaged as public authorities. Even with this insertion, the activities or transactions undertaken by the Central Government, State Government and a Local Authority, in which they are engaged as public authorities alone are to be excluded from the scope of 'business' for the purposes of this entry. This Explanation does not exclude a Government Entity and hence the situation remains unchanged even by the aforesaid insertion of explanation so far as the activity of the applicant is concerned. [Para 7.9]

In view of the foregoing, the following ruling is passed:

1.

The rate of tax applicable to the composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act undertaken by the applicant is to be charged at 9 per cent under the CGST Act and 9 per cent under the KGST Act, or at 18 per cent under the IGST Act.

2.

The amendments to the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, has no effect on the taxability of the transactions of the applicant as the transactions of the applicant are covered under item No. (ii) of Serial No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and are not covered under item No. (vi) of Serial No. 3 of the said Notification, as amended. [Para 8]

No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and taxable at 9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST

FACT: The applicant has entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences [NCBS] for the purpose of execution of works contract for construction of building for laboratories and associated facilities at NCBS Campus in Bangalore.

It sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

What is the applicable rate of tax for the provision of construction service rendered to NCBS.

HELD: The applicant is providing works contract service to NCBS and there is no dispute whatsoever that it is a works contract service as per clause (119) of section 2. [Para 5.2]

The NCBS has obtained registration under the GST Act as a trust and the council managing this organisation has three members appointed by the Government of India, one member appointed by the Government of Maharashtra, two members appointed by the trustees of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, the Director of the Institute (NCBS) is an ex-officio member and one co-opted member appointed by the council. Hence four members are from the Government. [Para 5.3]

The issue is whether the NCBS is covered under any one of the categories viz. Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. It is clear at the outset itself that NCBS is not Central Government or State Government or Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 5.4]

The argument of the applicant that the NCBS is covered under the category Government Authority cannot be accepted in the light of the definition of Governmental Authority in clause (ix) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017). [Para 5.5]

The only question that needs to be examined is whether NCBS is a Government Entity or not. Clause (x) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017) defines Government Entity as:

'Government Entity' means an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation,

(i)

Set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

Established by any Government,

with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 5.6]

From the above work details submitted by the applicant it is very clear that the entire contact is in the form of a composite contract consisting of supply of goods and services and where the main intention is to provide drinking water to the villages after removing excess Iron impurities and which therefore would be the main part of the contract. In view of the above discussions and also in view of the submissions made by the applicant, the work done by them is a composite supply which attracts the provisions of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. The said Notifications has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in Column 3 of the Table in the said Notfn, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein. Based on the above discussions, the relevant clause applicable to the subject case would be clauses (iii) of the said Notfn, as amended by Notfn No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-10-2017. A plain reading of Sr. No. 3, clause (iii) reveals that 'composite supply of WCS supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of, pipeline, conduit or plant for (i) water supply (ii) water treatment, or (iii) sewerage treatment or disposal attracts a tax rate of 6 per cent each of CGST and SGST. However, the benefit of 12 per cent tax rate would be available to the applicant only if the Works Contract services provided by them are Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of, pipeline, conduit or plant for (i) water supply (ii) water treatment. [Para 5]

In view of the extensive deliberations as held hereinabove TSH 9954 is applicable to the subject contract of extracting water from tube well, passing it through treatment plant of removing unwanted contaminants like iron from ground water and eventually lifting it to overhead tank and the same would attract a tax rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST and SGST). Question No. 36: Can a developer take deduction of actual value of land involved in sale of unit instead of taking deduction of deemed value of land as per Paragraph 2 to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017? Ans: No. Valuation mechanism prescribed in paragraph 2 of the notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 clearly prescribes one-third abatement towards value of land.

Therefore, the value of land or undivided share of land is deemed to be one-third of the total amount charged for the supply irrespective of the actual value of land and accordingly the applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of the total amount charged for the supply in arriving at the taxable value of the supply. [Para 11]

The next question raised by the applicant is whether the activity of purchase of land, development of the same into plots and sale of the same to various customers without collecting any advance from the customers for undertaking the development activities attract GST. The contention of the applicant is that the activity is sale of land and it is neither a supply of goods nor a supply of services as per Schedule III of the CGST Act. As per Paragraph 5(b) of Schedule II of the CGST Act construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly, except where the entire consideration has been received after issuance of completion certificate, where required by the competent authority or after its first occupation, whichever is earlier shall be treated as a supply of services. In the instant case, it is stated by the applicant that it is not receiving any advance from its customers for undertaking development activities in the plot and the plot is sold after development. Hence the transaction is in respect of sale of developed plots/land and is covered by Paragraph 5 of Schedule III of the CGST Act which stipulates that sale of land and, subject to clause (b) of paragraph 5 of Schedule II, sale of building shall be treated neither as a supply of goods nor a supply of service. Therefore, the transaction is not liable to GST. [Para 12]

Answer to question No. 3

The taxable value of the construction services supplied by the applicant shall be governed by the provisions of Para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and the applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of the total amount charged for the supply in arriving at the taxable value of the supply.

Answer to question No. 4

The sale of developed plots/land without receiving any advance from customers for undertaking development activities is covered by Para 5 of Schedule III of the CGST Act and it is neither a supply of goods nor a supply of service. Therefore, such sale is not liable to GST. [Para 13]

In the instant case the applicant is collecting amount from the member who is selling the site and that amount is kept as endowment fund. The applicant utilising the proceeds/accretions of the endowment fund for sourcing goods or service from the third person for the common use of its members. The exemption under Entry 77(c) of Notification No. 12/2017- Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 2/2018, dated 25-1-2018 is available only when the applicant receives the amount from its members as contribution or reimbursement against the amount paid by the applicant for sourcing of goods or services from the third person for common use of its members. Since the applicant is utilising the amount which is collected from the member who are selling their sites, such contribution is not for providing any maintenance services, instead he is providing no-objection certificates and other clearances for the site sellers. Hence this amount when collected amounts to a service and the applicant is liable to pay GST at the rate of 18% as such services are unclassified services covered under entry no. 35 of the Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. Hence, the contributions of the members who are selling the sites and obtaining clearances from the applicant for such sale, are liable to tax under the GST Acts.

Further, the endowment fund belongs to the applicant society and interest gets accrued to this fund. HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Madhya Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Applicant-company is engaged in carrying out works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, and civil structures - A company (MPPGCL) owned by Government of Madhya Pradesh, floated a tender, for construction of some flats - Applicant raised bill for work completed at rate of 18 per cent GST to MPPGCL - However, MPPGCL is of opinion that in work under reference, applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent by treating itself as a Government entity - Whether since Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in MPPGCL and is also exercising full control over activities of said company, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for purpose of GST - Held, yes - Whether since construction activity does not have any relation to principal work of power generation entrusted by State Government to MPPGCL, works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and Notification No. 11/2017-Madhya Pradesh Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [para 5] [In favour of respondent]GST: Where activity of construction of flats allotted by MPPGCL to applicant does not have any relation to principal work of power generation entrusted by State Government to MPPCGL, work contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST)

FACT: The applicant-company (MPPGCL) is engaged in carrying out the works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, civil structures of Government, semi-Government and private undertakings.

The applicant was awarded a contract for construction of 599 flats by MPPGCL.

During the course of carrying out the construction work, the applicant company raised Running Bills (RA bills) for the portion of work completed at a point of time to MPPGCL by charging CGST and SGST at the rate of 9 per cent each, in view of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017.

MPPGCL is of the opinion that in the work under reference, the applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent (6+6), as per Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, by treating itself as a Government entity and the work allocated to the service provider is the work which is the work supplied to it by the Government.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether MPPGCL is a 'Government Entity' and whether the work contract service of construction of 599 residential quarters allotted to the applicant company, will be charged under the GST rate of 12 per cent (6+6) or 18 per cent (9+9).

HELD: In the application itself it is stated that MPPGCL has been established by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in the company and is also exercising full control over the activities of the said company. Thus, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST law, as it fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions laid down under notification No. 11/2017. [Para 5.4]

commercial concerns for the purpose of residential leasing should be eligible for exemption under entry 12 of the Exemption Notification; the intention behind the said exemption is to provide relief from GST on residential dwelling. Accordingly, in order for the said objective to be fulfilled both legs of the transaction (i.e., renting of property by the applicant to a business entity and further renting of the property by the entity to the Tenants for use as residence) should be covered under the exemption.[Para 7.13] It is pertinent to mention here that the Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a transaction based tax, with seamless input tax credit at each transaction level. In the instant case two transactions are involved. The first being a transaction between the applicant and the business entity and the second between the business entity and the actual tenant. Thus the two transactions are different and the taxability/exemption of these transactions need to be examined individually. In the transaction between the applicant and business entity, the renting of residential dwelling is not for use as residence by the business entity but in the course or furtherance of the business of the said entity and hence the exemption under entry No. 12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 is not applicable to the impugned transaction. On the other hand in the transaction between the business entity and the tenant, the service amount to renting/leasing of rooming house which falls under accommodation services that get covered under SAC 996311 and hence the exemption under entry No. 12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 would not be applicable to the said transaction. [Para 7.14]

In view of the foregoing, it is ruled as follows

1. 'Leasing of property for use as residence along with basic amenities', in the instant case, is covered under accommodation services, as ruled in the preceding paras, falls under SAC 996311 and hence would qualify as composite supply under section 2(30).

2. Renting of property by applicant is not covered under entry 12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, as their services are covered under accommodation services falling under SAC 996311.

3. The exemption under entry 14 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 is available to the transaction of the applicant.

4. Leasing of property for residential subletting would not be covered under the exemption for residential dwelling under entry 12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as the two are different and individual transactions.[Para 8]

Classification of services - West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant is promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing a residential house project named 'Akriti' (RREP) - Whether works contract service received from contractors for construction of those dwelling units in project named 'Akriti' that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of said notification, provided applicant does not opt for paying tax at rate specified in Entry No. 3(ie) or Entry No. 3(if) - Held, yes [Para 4.10]GST : Where applicant who is promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing residential housing project 'Akriti', works contract service received from contractors for construction of those dwelling units that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of said notification, provided applicant does not opt for paying tax at rate specified in Entry No. 3(ie) Entry No. 3(if)

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) - Whether since control over BDA rests with Govt. of Karnataka, BDA is a Government entity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant involves supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and, hence, is a 'works contract' within meaning of section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether transaction of applicant would be a supply of works contract services covered under clause (a) of Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 10.8, 10.9.2  11]GST : Where applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), activity undertaken by applicant is supply of works contract service to a Govt. entity covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant entered into a contract with developer for construction of residential apartment - Applicant has not provided any evidence to effect that above project is covered under affordable housing project in terms of Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Whether if projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, contract of supply by applicant would be covered under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and at 6 per cent SGST and, otherwise said services will be liable to tax at rate of 9 per cent under CGST Act and at rate of 9 per cent under KGST Act as provided in Sl. Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - A charitable organisation 'S' engaged in various charitable activities across Kerala has awarded a rehabilitation project to applicant for providing affordable shelter to 2018 flood victims - Applicant constructed 45 residential units in different locations on land belonging to flood victims identified by Trust - Whether activity undertaken by applicant cannot be construed as construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer and, hence, rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is not applicable in respect of said activity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant is construction of 45 individual residential houses at different locations on land belonging to individual beneficiaries and activity squarely falls within scope of works contract as defined in section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether services provided by applicant to 'S' for construction of low cost housing units falls within ambit of Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 15]GST : Where applicant constructed residential units on land belonging to flood victims under a rehabilitation project awarded to it by a charitable trust, activity squarely falls within scope of works contract under section 2(119) and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Civil construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant-company is engaged in business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor - It seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether construction services proposed to be provided by applicant will qualify for reduced GST rate of 12 per cent as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Low cost houses in an affordable housing project having area of 60 sq. mts. or upto 60 sq. mts. will attract 12 per cent GST - Whether since project undertaken by applicant is an affordable housing project, it will attract rate of 12 per cent GST under Sr. No. 3 of said Notification – Held, yes [Para 5.8][In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant undertook project of construction of residential flat (Low cost flats) having carpet area of upto or less than 60 sq. mts. and its project falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing Project', applicant's case is covered under concessional tax rate slab of 12 per cent

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - State Police Housing and Infrastructure Corporation is a company of Government of Karnataka State incorporated under companies Act, 1956 and all shares are held by Government of Karnataka; hence, it qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for construction of International Center and Museum are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.2 and 14] [In favour of revenue] Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Karnataka Residential Educational Institutions Society (KRIES) is formed under societies Registration Act and Government of Karnataka may appoint persons to review progress of society and to hold inquiries into affairs of society and give directions; hence, qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for Construction of Residential school complex are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per Entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 03/2022 - Central Tax (Rate), dated : 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.3 and 14] [In favour of revenue] Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Works of construction of Airport Terminal Buildings/facilities and associated works awarded by Public Works Department of Government of Karnataka, are work supplied to State Government – However, said works for construction of airport terminal building or airport are predominantly meant for commerce and, hence, are not covered under Entry 3(iii),(vi),(ix) and (x) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Said works are covered under entry 3(xii) liable to 18 per cent tax [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.4 and 14] [In favour of revenue]   Circulars and Notifications : Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; Notification No. 15/2021 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 18-11-2021; Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021; and Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

Nos. 3(vi)(a) and (b) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) with applicable GST rate being 12 per cent - HELD : Impugned supply is in nature of composite supply of works contract service as it includes construction of school building, school and college hostels etc. - Impugned service is supplied to Gujarat Government - Activity undertaken is outside purview of business - School building is meant for use as an educational establishment as described in entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) - School building will be used by State Government for education and cannot be considered as commercial building - Impugned supply merits classification under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) attracting 12 per cent GST [Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 9, 10 and 11] [In favour of assessee]GST : Composite supply of works contract that includes construction of school building, school and college hostel, staff quarters, etc. provided to State Government is subject to 12% GST as it is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction service provided to National Centre for Biological Sciences - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant has entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences [NCBS] for purpose of execution of works contract for construction of building at NCBS Campus - NCBS is not Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity - Whether service supplied by applicant to NCBS is covered under item (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and taxable at 9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST - Held, yes [Para 6] [In favour of revenue]GST : Where applicant has entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences [NCBS] for purpose of execution of works contract for construction of building at NCBS Campus, service supplied by applicant to NCBS is covered under item (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and taxable at 9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Civil Construction and works contract services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)/Section 2(119) of the Central Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services - It has entered into agreement to undertake subcontract work of civil construction of residential complexes/row of residential houses which in turn has been allotted to GIPL (main contractor) through tender by Bengaluru Development Authority - Whether since projects of applicant are involving supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property it is a 'work contract' within meaning of section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether works contract is for construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and it is covered under clause (a) of entry 3(vi) of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether further, since main contractor is providing services specified in item 3(vi) of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, subcontract work of works contract provided by applicant as a subcontractor to main contractor is covered under item (ix) of entry 3 of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, taxable at 6 per cent CGST with effect from 25-1-2018 - Whether however, for period from 1-7-2017 to 24-1-2018, same is taxable at 9 per cent CGST - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 12]GST: Projects of applicant involving work orders from Principal contractor for civil construction of residential complexes consisting of supply of both goods and services in relation to an immovable property is a 'works contract' within meaning of section 2(119)   GST: Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Entity within meaning of Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 - Works contract - Applicant entered into a construction contract for construction of fish market building and sought advance ruling on whether activity of composite supply of works contract service by way of construction of fish market for Panchayat (Road and Building) Division, Valsad District Panchayat merits classification at Serial Number 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-17(NT) - It is found that to be eligible to be covered vide 3(vi)(a) of said Notification, supply shall be composite supply of works contract, supply shall be to Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Government Authority or a Government Entity and civil structure or original works must predominantly be meant for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession - It is found that subject contract is for construction of immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods is involved in execution of subject contract and subject supply is a composite supply of works contract service - Further, service recipient is a Local Authority and activity squarely falls under entry no 22 'Markets and Fairs' of Eleventh Schedule to Constitution - Whether therefore, activity of composite supply of works contract service by way of construction of fish market for Panchayat (Road and Building) Division, Valsad District Panchayat merits classification at Serial Number 3(vi)(a) of said NT and is eligible for 12 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 7, 8, 14 and 15]GST : Activity of composite supply of works contract service by way of construction of fish market for Panchayat (Road and Building) Division, Valsad District Panchayat merits classification at Serial Number 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is eligible for 12 per cent GST

No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017  GST : Where applicant, engaged in business of civil works contract entered into an agreement with developer for construction of residential apartment project, since contract is for construction of an immovable property, same is covered under works contract as per section 2(119)

Slum infrastructure - Construction service - Works contract service for State Slum Development Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for Karnataka Slum Development Board under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana as a main contractor are liable to 12 per cent GST till 17-7-2022, in terms of Sl. No. 3(iv)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification Nos. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and thereafter, such services are liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl.
