Construction service - Affordable residential apartment - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Residential Real Estate Project (RREP) comprised of both affordable and other than affordable residential apartments - HELD : Project undertaken is covered under definition of 'real estate project' and applicant falls within definition of a 'promoter' - Construction of affordable residential apartments is covered under services specified in entry at Sl. No. 3(i) and (ia) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - GST is payable at 1.5 per cent in respect of service of construction of affordable residential apartments and at 7.5 per cent in respect of service of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments [Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.7 and 7.8] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars  Notifications : Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Construction services (NR) - Applicant is engaged in business of construction of residential and commercial complex - Applicant is undertaking development of residential apartments under a project called 'Prajapati Magnum' - Whether since project undertaken by applicant falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing', applicant's case is covered under tax rate of 12 per cent, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services) of Notification No. 11/2017 but benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018, i.e., date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable in case of only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6]CGST: Where project 'Prajapati Magnum' undertaken by applicants falls under definition of Affordable Housing, GST at rate of 12 per cent will be leviable on construction of low cost houses with carpet area upto 60 sq. m.

Works contract service - Construction of employee quarters - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Whether execution of works contract service for construction of residential quarters for employees of Kudankulam Nuclear Power Project (KKNPP) which is unit of Nuclear Power Corporation India Limited (NPCIL) would be taxable at 12 per cent - HELD : Works contract service is provided as is evident from contract - NPCIL qualifies as government entity as it has been established under Department of Atomic Energy with 100 per cent equity held by Central Government - Work entrusted to NPCIL is to implement atomic power projects for generation of electricity - Construction of residential quarters for KKNPP cannot be construed as work in relation to work entrusted to NPCIL by Central Government in absence of any document providing for same - Impugned works contract service is not covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) and concessional rate of 12 per cent is not available - GST is payable at 18 per cent in terms of entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) - Concessional rate of 12 per cent will not be available even if service rendered is in relation to work entrusted by government entity as said term was omitted from 1-1-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.3, 7.4, 7.5, 8 and 10] [In favour of revenue]GST : Concessional rate of 12 per cent GST is not available to works contract service rendered to government entity when same is not in relation to work entrusted by government till 31-12-2021 and even otherwise after 1-1-2022 such activity is liable to GST of 18 per cent  GST : Advance ruling cannot be sought on questions that are purely procedural in nature

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Applicant a Private Limited Company entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences(NCBS) for construction of Hostel building at NCBS Campus in Bangalore - It sought advance ruling on whether it should charge GST at rate of 12 per cent for service provided to NCBS as per Notification No 24/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 21-9-2017- It is found that NCBS, which is a separate centre of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), receives grant from Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India and that NCBS is neither set-up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature nor was established by any Government, but is an autonomous body under aegis of TIFR - Moreover, council administering this institute has only 4 members appointed by Government and therefore Government does not have more than 90 per cent control over it - Thus, NCBS is not covered under definition of a 'Government Entity' as per clause (x) of para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Furthermore, Institute is not established to carry out a function entrusted by Government, thus, it is not covered by clause (vi) of serial no. 3 of Notification - Whether therefore, service supplied by applicant to NCBS is not taxable at concessional rate of 12 per cent and is taxable at 18 per cent under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6]GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

Construction of residential apartments in a Residential Real Estate Project - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Applicant has acquired a piece of land and developed same into a layout - It has entered into MoU with prospective buyers for purchase of land and construction of residential house - Two separate agreements with buyer is entered, one for sale of plot (sale deed) and other for construction of residential house - Signing of MoU and execution of two agreements on same day implies that construction service provided by applicant to buyers is a single contract for sale of land and construction of building - HELD : Activity rendered by applicant is in nature of 'original works' since applicant is constructing a new building - Project being undertaken by applicant is a residential real estate project (RREP) as no commercial apartments are constructed in project - Activity of applicant would fall under Entry No. 3(i) and 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and conditions mentioned should be strictly adhered to for claiming benefit of said Notification - Applicant is eligible to claim Entry No. 3(i) and 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate) and liable to pay GST at rate of 1.5 per cent in respect of construction of affordable residential apartments and at rate of 7.5 per cent for construction of apartments other than affordable residential apartments - Further, taxable value for Construction services supplied by applicant is governed by provisions of Para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) r/ w Notification No. 11/2017-ST (Rate) as amended - Accordingly, applicant is eligible to avail only deduction of one-third of total amount charged for supply for arriving at taxable value of supply [Section 9, read with section 11, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 23][In favour of Revenue]  Circulars and Notifications: Circular DOF No. 334/1/12010-TRU dated 26-022010, TRU's letter F. No. 354/32/2019-TRU dated 7th May, 2019, Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) r/w Notification No. 11/2017-ST(Rate)

Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of affordable residential apartments/Construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments - Heading 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant is engaged in promotion of gated community villas for prospective villa buyers - It buys land and divides same into plots and sells plots to villa buyers - While booking of plots happens, it enters into construction agreement with villa buyers to construct and transfer villa to villa buyers on payment of agreed consideration as per agreed conditions in construction agreement - In certain cases applicant develops projects that are uncompleted by other developers and constructs villas for prospective villa buyers - Whether applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 1.5 per cent [0.75 per cent CGST + 0.75 per cent SGST] in respect of services of construction of affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (i) and at rate of 7.5 per cent [3.75 per cent CGST + 3.75 per cent SGST] in respect of services of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 subject to conditions prescribed under respective entries in villa projects - Held, yes - Whether applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 1.5 per cent [0.75 per cent CGST + 0.75 per cent SGST] in respect of services of construction of affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (i) and at rate of 7.5 per cent [3.75 per cent CGST + 3.75 per cent SGST] in respect of services of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 subject to conditions prescribed under respective entries in redeveloped projects undertaken by it after 1-4-2019 - Held, yes [Para 13]GST : Where applicant is engaged in promotion of gated community villas for prospective villa buyers and it buys land and divides same into plots and sells plots to villa buyers and while booking of plots happens it enters into construction agreement with villa buyers to construct and transfer villa to villa buyers on payment of agreed consideration as per agreed conditions in construction agreement, applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 1.5 per cent in respect of services of construction of affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (i) and at rate of 7.5 per cent in respect of services of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 subject to conditions prescribed under respective entries in villa projects  GST : Where applicant is engaged in promotion of gated community villas for prospective villa buyers and it buys land and divides same into plots and sells plots to villa buyers and while booking of plots happens it enters into construction agreement with villa buyers to construct and transfer villa to villa buyers on payment of agreed consideration as per agreed conditions in construction agreement, taxable value of construction services supplied by applicant shall be governed by provisions of Para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and it is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of total amount charged for supply in arriving at taxable value of supply   GST : Where applicant is engaged in promotion of gated community villas for prospective villa buyers and it buys land in its own name and develops land and after getting lay-out approvals in its name sells plots to various prospective buyers without any construction activities, sale of developed plots/land by applicant without receiving any advance from customers for undertaking development activities is neither supply of goods nor a supply of services

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Works of construction of Airport Terminal Buildings/facilities and associated works awarded by Public Works Department of Government of Karnataka, are work supplied to State Government – However, said works for construction of airport terminal building or airport are predominantly meant for commerce and, hence, are not covered under Entry 3(iii),(vi),(ix) and (x) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Said works are covered under entry 3(xii) liable to 18 per cent tax [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.4 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

Construction services - Tax Liability - Applicant is engaged in business of providing construction services in respect of commercial or residential buildings and civil structures - Applicant seeks advance ruling on whether applicant can levy and discharge output tax on services provided by it at effective rate of 8 per cent (12 per cent less 1/3rd value deducted on account of land) under entry No. 3(ie) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 - HELD : Aforesaid notification, is applicable, if construction of residential units is less than 60 sq. mts. and construction should not be for commercial purposes - In instant case, applicant has stated that all units are below 60 sq. mts. and has submitted project plans and unit configuration of 'Block 7' in support of same - Further, applicant has stated that area of commercial unit is less than 15 per cent of total area of project - From a reading of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended, aforesaid notification is applicable to applicant - In this regard, aforesaid item is applicable to applicant and rates as mentioned against entry item 'i.e.' shall be applicable to applicant, which is 12 per cent (CGST 6 per cent + SGST 6 per cent) - Further, in case of supply of services involves transfer of land or undivided share of land, value of supply shall be reduced by 1/3rd, making effective rate 8 per cent (CGST 4 per cent + SGST 4 per cent) [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6.13-7] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications : Circular F. No. 354/32/2019-TRU, dated 7-5-2019, Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019

Section 2(30), read with section 8, of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(30), read with section 8, of the West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Supply - Composite supply - Applicant is developing a residential housing project 'A' and supplying construction service to recipients - In addition to construction service, it will provide services like preferential location service, car packing services, etc. - Whether since applicant is providing service of construction of a dwelling unit in a residential complex, bundled with services relating to preferential location of unit and right to use car parking space and common areas and facilities, it is a composite supply - Held, yes - Whether construction service being principal supply, entire value of composite supply is to be treated, for purpose of taxation, as supply of construction service, taxable under Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 4.7]   Circulars and Notifications : Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 and Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 West Bengal State (Rate) dated 28-6-2017  (NR)

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of independent houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Applicant has entered into a sub-contract agreement for execution of works contract pertaining to construction of independent houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana with main contractor, who has been awarded contract - Whether sub-contract of construction of independent houses by applicant under main contract of construction of houses pertaining to Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana is covered under sub-item (c) of item (iv) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to CGST at 6 per cent + SGST at 6 per cent - Held, yes [Para 6] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where applicant has entered into a sub-contract agreement for execution of works contract pertaining to construction of independent houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana with main contractor, who has been awarded contract, sub-contract is covered under sub-item (c) of item (iv) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to CGST at 6 per cent + SGST at 6 per cent

Slum infrastructure - Construction service - Works contract service for State Slum Development Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for Karnataka Slum Development Board under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana as a main contractor are liable to 12 per cent GST till 17-7-2022, in terms of Sl. No. 3(iv)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification Nos. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and thereafter, such services are liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(ix) and liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of said Notification [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 to 12 and 16 to 18]GST : Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for State Slum Development Board under Government Scheme as a main contractor is liable to 12 per cent GST till 17-7-2022 and thereafter, to 18 per cent GST; however, these services when provided by sub-contractor are also liable to 18 per cent GST  GST : Construction services provided to State Housing Board with respect to construction of Police Station as a main contractor/sub-contractor are liable to 18 per cent GST  GST : Construction services provided to a SPV of State Government and Municipal Corporation, for development of market under smart city project are liable to 18 per cent GST irrespective of whether such services are provided by main contractor or sub-contractor

Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Housing Project construction -  Heading 9954 - [Construction services] - Applicant has entered into civil construction contract with 'J' Ltd. in respect of seven residential buildings - Whether since project undertaken by applicant falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing Project' (carpet area being less than 60 sq. Mts.) applicant's case is covered under concessional tax rate of 12 per cent under Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) in terms of item (v)(da) of Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017, Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, benefit of reduced rate would be available to applicant in cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018, i.e. date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued for those flats having carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. - Held, yes - Whether, however, in case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. or which are commercial units, applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate - Held, yes - Whether building completion and finishing services will not be regarded as a separate services; such building completion and finishing services will be a part of composite supply of works contract services with principal supply of building construction - Held,yes - Whether 'housing project' cannot be confined only to dwelling units, it would also include within its fold, other common amenities, structures, etc. and, thus, rate applicable to principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities - Held, yes - Whether rate of GST will be 18% on works contract services provided for construction of units, common areas and amenities which do not qualify criteria of low cost houses - Held, yes [Paras 5.11, and 5.14.2][In favour of assessee]GST : Where applicant constructs residential complex under contract and project undertaken by it falls under definition of ‘affordable housing project’ (carpet area being less than 60 sq. Mts.), applicant’s case is covered under Heading No. 9954 eligible for concessional tax rate of 12 per cent; in case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. or which are commercial units, applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate

Construction service - Affordable residential apartment (ARA) - Heading 9954 - Concessional rate of tax - Vacant housing plots are approved by Sembakkam Municipality by collecting necessary fees - However, necessary fees towards development charges are collected by CMDA which means planning authority is CMDA - HELD : Though Sembakkam Municipality is 'appropriate local body' for issuing approval order for building plan, necessary fees towards 'development charges' were collected by Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) - Planning authority for impugned project is CMDA and by extension, impugned project falls within ambit of Metropolitan City of Chennai - Same cannot be considered as located in city or town 'other than Metropolitan Cities' in terms of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras5.6,5.8 and 5.9] [In favour of revenue]   Circulars  Notifications : Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Karnataka Residential Educational Institutions Society (KRIES) is formed under societies Registration Act and Government of Karnataka may appoint persons to review progress of society and to hold inquiries into affairs of society and give directions; hence, qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for Construction of Residential school complex are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per Entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 03/2022 - Central Tax (Rate), dated : 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.3 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Whether dwelling units measuring less than 60 sq. mtrs. will qualify as low cost houses; they are eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 with effect from 25-1-2018 - Held, yes - Whether concessional rate of 12 per cent, would be available only in respect of society formation charges, club house development charges, water, electricity, drainage, sewerage charges legal service charges and documentation charges, which are collected from buyers of houses having area less than 60 sq. mtrs. - Held, yes - Applicant, a real estate developer in India is involved in a residential development project under name 'Joyville Virar' - Applicant is seeking advance ruling in respect of dwelling units at Joyville to qualify as low cost houses eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 with effect from 25-1-2018 - Whether project of applicant qualifies as an 'ongoing project under Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and applicant is eligible for concessional rate of benefit under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended, only for dwelling units measuring less than 60 sq. mtrs. - Held, yes - Whether however, units which do not qualify criteria of 'low cost houses' will be taxed at 18 per cent GST - Held, yes [Para 6]GST : Dwelling units measuring less than 60 sq. mtrs. will qualify as low cost houses and they are eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST under Entry No. 3 (v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Kerala State Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)- Section 2(119), of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per tender requirements - They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for construction of a building for space transportation system - It is a composite contract which includes supply of materials as well as service - They have also received another work order from Infrastructure Kerala Ltd., a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for development of Medical College which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Applicant has requested for advance ruling on rate of tax applicable for above works contracts awarded by Government authorities - Whether since services provided by applicant under both contracts fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services are being provided to Central Government and State Government, applicant is eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Held, yes [Para 9]GST: Where services of construction with material provided by applicant under construction contracts awarded by Government authorities fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services being provided to Central and State government, applicant will be eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3 (vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017, dated 28-6-2017

Construction services - Tax Liability - Applicant is engaged in business of providing construction services in respect of commercial or residential buildings and civil structures - Applicant seeks advance ruling on whether applicant can levy and discharge output tax on services provided by it at effective rate of 8 per cent (12 per cent less 1/3rd value deducted on account of land) under entry No. 3(ie) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 - HELD : Aforesaid notification, is applicable, if construction of residential units is less than 60 sq. mts. and construction should not be for commercial purposes - In instant case, applicant has stated that all units are below 60 sq. mts. and has submitted project plans and unit configuration of 'Block 7' in support of same - Further, applicant has stated that area of commercial unit is less than 15 per cent of total area of project - From a reading of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended, aforesaid notification is applicable to applicant - In this regard, aforesaid item is applicable to applicant and rates as mentioned against entry item 'i.e.' shall be applicable to applicant, which is 12 per cent (CGST 6 per cent + SGST 6 per cent) - Further, in case of supply of services involves transfer of land or undivided share of land, value of supply shall be reduced by 1/3rd, making effective rate 8 per cent (CGST 4 per cent + SGST 4 per cent) [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6.13-7] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where applicant-assessee has stated that all units for which they provide construction services, are below 60 sq. mts. and area of commercial unit is less than 15 per cent of total area of project, therefore, sub-item (da) of item (v), of entry number 3(ie) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable to applicant-assessee and rate of 12 per cent shall be applicable; in case of supply of services involves transfer of land or undivided share of land value of supply, tax liability shall be reduced by 1/3rd, making effective rate at 8 per cent

Residential apartment construction - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional Rate - Applicant-real estate developer has purchased land in its name and has obtained building permit - It has entered into two agreements with customers; one for sale of undivided share of land and another for construction of apartment - GST is not collected on amount collected for undivided share of land but same was collected for apartment construction at rate of 18 per cent - Applicant's project is satisfying all conditions of definition of 'ongoing project' as occurring in clause (xx) of Para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 - Applicant is eligible and has exercised its option for continuing with payment of tax at old rates in respect of ongoing projects - Project is not covered under any of schemes specified under Item (ie) of Sl. No. 3 of said notification - Therefore, applicant is not eligible for concessional rate of tax at 12 per cent - Applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 18 per cent in respect of services of construction of residential apartments supplied by it [Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.10] [In favour of revenue]GST : Applicant-real estate developer having exercised its option for continuing with payment of tax at old rates in respect to its ongoing project of construction of residential apartments should pay GST at rate of 18 per cent; since project is not covered under any of schemes specified under Item (ie) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), applicant is not eligible for concessional rate of tax of 12 per cent  GST : Where applicant is providing construction of residential apartment services alongwith sale of an undivided share of land in arriving at taxable value of supply, applicant will be eligible to avail deduction of one-third of total amount (being deemed value of undivided share of land) charged for supply   GST : Provisions of section 13 of CGST, 2017 will apply to determination of time of supply of construction of residential apartments services

Construction and commission of jetty/berth - Construction is executed services - Heading No. 9954 - Exemption - Project for Indian Coast Guard (ICG) - Contraction is executed by Cochin Port Trust (COPT) (applicant), established by Central Government under Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 with 100 per cent of its control - Applicant is taking up relevant studies, approvals/clearances, turnkey design, and all actions for execution, including engaging independent contractors - All costs met by ICG on basis of actual cost of construction Contractors/suppliers would raise invoice on applicant which in turn would raise invoices on ICG - HELD : Applicant's activities are 'works contract' under section 2(119) of CGST Act, 2017 and supply as per Sl. No. 6(a) of Schedule II thereof - Applicant is Government entity as defined in Para 2(zfa) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Indian Coast Guard is Central Government - Hence, two conditions in Sl. No. 9C of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), as inserted by Notification No. 32/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017, are satisfied - However, as there is no record that consideration for services received by applicant is grant from Central Government, fourth condition in Sl. No. 9C of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) is not satisfied - Hence, service provided by applicant to ICG is not eligible for exemption under entry at Sl. No. 9C of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - As works contract services are provided to Central Government for ICG's activities as public authority, concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent is eligible under Entry at Item (vi) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - However, as entry at Item (vi) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) has been omitted by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 with effect from 18-7-2022, concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent is applicable only in respect of services supplied between 21-9-2017 and 17-7-2022 [Section 9, read with  section 2(119), of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.11, 7.17, 7.18 and 7.22] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Construction and commission of jetty/berth by applicant port trust 'COPT' for Indian Coast Guard (ICG) is supply of 'works contract'; as consideration for services received by COPT is grants from Central Government, condition in Sl. No. 9C of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) is not satisfied and COPT is not eligible for exemption; as services are provided to Central Government for ICG's activities as public authority, applicant will be eligible to concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent under entry at Item (vi) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) for services supplied between 21-9-2017 and 17-7-2022  GST : Advance Ruling cannot be granted on applicant's eligibility to refund of excess tax paid and taxability of services provided by their contractors, as these questions are out of purview of advance ruling definition and section 97(2) of CGST Act, 2017

Section  9 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section  9 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Levy and collection of tax -  Applicant is engaged in construction of residential complex in two parts i. e. Part-A and Part-B - It seeks advance ruling on question as to whether it is eligible for benefit of reduced rate of tax available in respect of houses constructed in Part-B with a carpet area of 60 not more then sq. meters per house - It is noted that Part-B of township can not be considered as a standalone housing projects since it shares common land, common facilities and common entrance with Part-A of township and 50 percent of FAR/FSI of entire housing project has not been used for construction of dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 sq. meters as per requirements of Notification No. 13/06/2009 dated 30-03-2017 of Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs - Hence , housing project in question can not be considered as an "affordable housing project" - Whether in view of aforesaid, it can be concluded that applicant has not fulfilled condition as envisaged in Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No.11/2017 CT (Rate) dated 28-06-2017 as amended by Notification No.01/2018 CT(Rate) dated 25-01-2018 , and, consequently benefit of reduced rate of tax is not available to applicant in respect of houses constructed with a carpet area of 60 sq. meters - Held, yes [Paras 10.2 and 10.3] [In favour of revenue]GST : Where applicant is engaged in construction of residential complex in two parts i.e. Part-A and Part-B, in view of fact that 50 per cent or more of FAR/FSI of entire housing project comprising of Part-A and Part-B has not been used for construction of dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 sq. meters., applicant is not eligible for benefit of reduced rate of tax as provided under Entry3(v)(da) of Notification No.11/2017 CT( Rate) dated 28-06-2017 as amended by Notification No.01/2018 CT(Rate) dated 25-01-2018

Construction of cultural complex - Construction Services - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Applicant provides works contract services of supply of materials, and labour for executing works - Assessee entered into agreement with State film development corporation for development and construction of cultural complex - HELD : State film development corporation is a public sector undertaking established by government of Kerala for promotion of Malyalam cinema in state - It falls under definition of 'government authority' as is fully under control of Government of Kerala and established for purpose listed under Sl. No. 21 of eleventh schedule of constitution - Furthermore, works contract services are performed by applicant as per contracts awarded by State film development corporation to construct a cultural complex is in nature of construction of structure meant for predominantly use as a cultural establishment and is liable to GST at 12 per cent as per Sl. 3(vi)(b) of Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.16 and 7.19] [In favour of assessee]GST : Works contract services performed by assessee as per contracts awarded by Kerela State film development corporation Ltd, a government authority to construct a cultural complex is in nature of construction of structure meant predominantly for use as a cultural establishment and is liable to GST at 12 per cent as per Sl 3(vi)(b) of Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

Reconstruction of jetty - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - "Works Contract" by government authority to government - Cochin Port Trust (CoPT) is established by Central Government under Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 with its 100% control - No document on record shows that consideration for services of jetty reconstruction for Indian Navy are received by CoPT as grants from Central Government - HELD : CoPT is Government entity as defined in Para 2 (zfa) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Indian Navy is a part of Central Government - Contract is Works Contract - Hence, three conditions of Sl. No. 9C of Notification ibid are satisfied - However, as consideration for services are not grants from Central Government, fourth condition of Sl. No. 9C of Notification ibid is not satisfied, and accordingly, service provided by CoPT is not eligible for exemption under this Sl. No. - However, as works contract services are provided to Central Government and meant for use of Indian Navy as public authority, they are eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12% as per entry at item (vi) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended; however, as this entry has been omitted by Notification No. 03/2022 Central Tax (Rate) dated 13-7-2022 with effect from 18-7-2022, concessional rate of GST of 12% is applicable only for services supplied between 21-9-2017 and 17-7-2022, and services supplied on or after 18-7-2022 will be liable to GST @ 18% as per entry at Item (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 [Major Port Trusts Act, 1963/Para 2 (zfa) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017/Items (vi) and (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017/Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 with effect from 18-7-2022] [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.11, 7.18, 7.22]

Housing construction - Construction service - Works contract service for State Housing Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction services are provided to Karnataka Housing Board with respect to construction of Police Station as a main contractor/sub-contractor - Karnataka Housing Board having been established under Karnataka Housing Board Act, 1962 and carrying out functions entrusted by State Government is to be considered as Government Entity as defined under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 and liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 13, 14 and 16 to 18]

Construction Service - Hospital of government entity - Heading 9954 - Classification - Whether service of construction of 200 bedded hospital to be provided to Uttar Pradesh Rajkiya Nirman Nigam Ltd., (UPRNN) is eligible for concessional rate of GST at 12% in terms of S. No. 3 (vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Applicant is required to construct entire hospital for Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) - Composite supply of works contract by way of construction of a hospital i.e., clinical establishment is provided to government entity - HELD : Service is eligible for concessional rate when they are provided to Union territory or local authority and is not eligible for concessional rate if provided to governmental authority or government entity as per amendment to Notification No. 11/2017 by Notification No. 15/2021 - Service to be provided is not covered under said entry of Notification No. 11/2017 providing for 12% GST rate and same will be covered under residuary clause (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 attracting 18% GST [Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5.2, 5.3.2, 5.3.3, 5.3.5, 5.4.1 and 5.4.2] [In favour of revenue]GST : Service of construction of hospital to be provided to a government entity is not covered under amended entry pertaining to concessional rate of 12% GST; such service attracts 18% GST

Community Centre maintained by Home Owners' Association - Membership organisation's service - Heading No. 9995 - Exemption - Applicant Home Owners' Association operated Community Centre within residential complex providing recreational facilities to residents and guests - Area was restricted to residents and did not engage in commercial activities with public at large - Overall control rested with Management Committee - Fixed monthly subscription for upkeep was decided in AGM/GBM and was mandatory irrespective of usage - Applicant sought inclusion within monthly maintenance for Entry 77 of Notification 12/2017-CTR exemption threshold - HELD : Services of Community Centre were integral to residential complex and were rendered exclusively to members - Such services were classifiable under Heading 9995, SAC 999598 as Home Owners Association - On conjoint reading of Notification 12/2017-CTR and Circular 109/28/2019-GST, monthly subscription toward upkeep formed part of maintenance charges - Exemption up to Rs 7,500 per member per month applied where amount represented inclusive value of maintenance for entire complex - Accordingly such charges shared same exemption treatment as other monthly maintenance collections [Section 11, read with section 7 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 17.3 and 17.6] [In favour of assessee]

Fire-fighting installation with pump house -  Construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly - Heading No. 9954 - Exemption - Appellant-assessee is a partnership firm and a civil contractor engaged in construction of roads, buildings, civil structures or various other civil works as awarded from various Governmental and non-Governmental organizations - AAR has held that appellant, is liable to pay GST at rate 18 per cent - What will be GST rate for work undertaken by appellant for service recipient under bid - HELD : It is observed that services provided by appellant are covered under Item number (vi) in Column (3) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Therefore, said services are liable to attract GST at 12 per cent (i.e. 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST) during contracted period only up to 31-12-2021, as after that, in Column No. (3) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 words 'Governmental authority or a Government entity' has been omitted vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax(Rate), dated 31-12-2021 with effect from 1-1-2022 [Section 11 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para11] [Partly in favour of assessee]

Real estate project - Construction service - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Applicant proprietary concern is owner of land - They have entered into a joint development agreement (JDA) and Supplementary Agreement with developer for development of residential apartments - Cost of construction shall be borne by Developer - Applicant would get 32 per cent share of apartments - HELD : Applicant is liable to pay tax as per entries 3(i) to 3(id) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 depending on nature of apartment, whether it is a residential or commercial apartment; if apartment is a residential apartment, whether it is affordable category or not and whether project is a residential real estate project or a real estate project other than residential real estate project [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 14] [In favour of revenue]

facts.text:
The applicant is engaged in the business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services. The applicant has applied for the civil construction work tender with Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) with respect to construction of residential complexes/row of residential houses.

The said project is allotted to the applicant and the same has been executed by the Company through appointing various contractors.

The applicant has sought advance ruling in respect of the question as to whether the activity undertaken by the applicant is covered under section 2(119); whether Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Authority as per the provisions of GST Law and the rate of tax applicable to the transaction of the applicant and more so whether the transactions are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended).

According to applicant, its activity of construction of residential house and residential complex with respect to following BDA projects (to Government Authority) are squarely covered under the definition of Works Contract and their activity will be considered as supply of services.

The applicant submits that as per the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), the activity undertaken by the applicant to BDA i.e., Government Authority is liable for GST at 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST.

The applicant-company is engaged in the business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor. It had filed the instant application in respect of a proposed civil construction contract to be entered into with a developer for construction of a residential project comprising of 135 buildings all having residential flats/units having carpet area of up to or less than 60 Sq. Mts. According to them, since more than 50 per cent of PSI is utilized towards construction of LCH, the project would qualify as an 'Affordable Housing Project' (AHP).

It seeks advance ruling on the issue as to whether the construction services proposed to be provided by the applicant will qualify for the reduced CGST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST), as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

The applicant-company (MPPGCL) is engaged in carrying out the works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, civil structures of Government, semi-Government and private undertakings.

The applicant was awarded a contract for construction of 599 flats by MPPGCL.

During the course of carrying out the construction work, the applicant company raised Running Bills (RA bills) for the portion of work completed at a point of time to MPPGCL by charging CGST and SGST at the rate of 9 per cent each, in view of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017.

MPPGCL is of the opinion that in the work under reference, the applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent (6+6), as per Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, by treating itself as a Government entity and the work allocated to the service provider is the work which is the work supplied to it by the Government.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether MPPGCL is a 'Government Entity' and whether the work contract service of construction of 599 residential quarters allotted to the applicant company, will be charged under the GST rate of 12 per cent (6+6) or 18 per cent (9+9).

The applicant CMRL, registered under the GST has acquired a land for public purpose and sought Advance Ruling on whether amount received for the purpose of granting right to access to the pathway leading to the dwelling unit is exempted from levy of GST as per the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, treating the agreement as one for leasing out a 'dwelling unit'.

The applicant is the promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing a residential housing project named 'Akriti' (RREP).

The applicant wants to know whether Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (Rate Notification), as amended time-to-time, applies to the works contract service received from the contractors.

The applicant (M.P. Power Generating Co. Ltd.) is 100 per cent Madhya Pradesh State Government hold company.

The State Government of Madhya Pradesh awarded a contract to the applicant to construct a Thermal Power Project.

Further the applicant has awarded a contract to one Shreeji Infrastructure India (P.) Ltd. towards construction of certain residential quarters at aforesaid Thermal Power Project.

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

-

Rate of GST on contract for construction of building and structure for colony at Thermal Power Project as per Notification No. 11/2017 as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 and further amended vide Notification No. 31/2017.

-

Rate of GST on construction contract of residential quarters at various power houses of the applicant as per Notification No. 11/2017 as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 and further amended vide Notification No. 31/2017.

The applicant submitted before the Authority for Advance Ruling that Shreeji Infrastructure India (P.) Ltd. has obtained an advance ruling on the issue raised in the instant application vide order No. 15/2018, dated 18-10-2018, but this fact was not brought to the notice of the Authority that the work is being entrusted to the applicant by Government of Madhya Pradesh and hence the applicant is filing a fresh advance ruling application.

The applicant, namely, City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Limited [CIDCO] proposes to transfer by way of lease vacant plots of Maharashtra State Government to (a) Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC) for use as Indoor Recreation Centre and Slaughter House, and (b) Panvel Municipal Corporation (PMC) for use as (i) PMC Ward Office(s), (ii) PMC Commissioner's residence, and (iii) PMC Mayor's residence.

It sought advance ruling in respect of the following questions:

(1) Whether the supply of services by the applicant, of 'transfer by way of lease' of vacant plots of 'Maharashtra State Government owned lands' or 'privately owned lands acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 by the Maharashtra State Government' vested in CIDCO, to:

(a)

Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC), for intended development thereof and construction of buildings by the latter on each of those plots, demarcated for separate use as:

(i)

Indoor Recreation Centre,

(ii)

Slaughter House;

(b)

Panvel Municipal Corporation (PMC), for intended development thereof and construction of buildings by the latter on each of those plots, demarcated for separate use as:

(i)

PMC Ward Office(s),

(ii)

PMC Commissioner's residence, and

(iii)

PMC Mayor's residence;

Meanwhile, the Karnataka State Screening Committee on Anti-profiteering received 3 more applications alleging that the Respondent had not passed on the benefit of ITC to them. These applications had also been forwarded to the Standing Committee who forwarded it to the DGAP for investigation as to whether the respondent had passed on the benefit of ITC by way of commensurate reduction in price, on implementation of GST with effect from 1-7-2017 or not.

The DGAP in his report has concluded that the applicable tax rate on construction service had increased from 8.02 per cent in the pre-GST period to 12 per cent in the post-GST period. The DGAP has further contended that there was an increase in the rate of tax and there was no additional benefit of ITC with the implementation of GST with effect from 1-7-2017, hence the provisions of section 171 were not attracted.

The applicant filed an application before Anti-Profiteering Authority stating that the respondent had resorted to profiteering in respect of the purchase of flat, constructed by the respondent in its 'Vrindavan Yojna Project', Lucknow.

The applicants had further alleged that the respondent had increased the price of the flat after implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) with effect from 1-7-2017 and had not passed on the benefit of Input Tax Credit (ITC) by way of commensurate reduction in the price of the flat purchased by them. They had also claimed that the respondent had committed contravention of the provisions of section 171 and, hence, appropriate action should be taken against them.

The DGAP found that the applicants had booked a flat with the respondent on 1-5-2017, before coming into force of the GST. The DGAP had also found that the applicants had bought the flat from the respondent for Rs. 61,80,747 including Service Tax at the rate of 4.5 per cent before coming into force of the GST and after its implementation the respondent had increased the price of the flat by Rs. 4,48,030 by charging GST at the rate of 12 per cent on the total payment. He had further found that the respondent had not passed on the benefit of ITC availed by him. He had also noticed that 85 per cent to 90 per cent of the construction had been completed at the time of booking of the flat.

The DGAP stated that the ITC as a percentage of the total turnover that was available to the respondent during the pre-GST period from April, 2016 to June, 2017 was 0.27 per cent and during the post-GST period with effect from July, 2017 to August, 2018, it was 3.31 per cent which confirmed that post-GST, the respondent had benefited from additional ITC to the extent of 3.04 per cent [3.31 per cent - 0.27 per cent] of the total turnover.

The DGAP had stated that the benefit of additional ITC of 3.04 per cent of the taxable turnover available during the period between 1-7-2017 to 31-8-2018 and the amount outstanding as on 31-8-2018, which had accrued to the respondent was required to be passed on to the applicants and the other recipients, however, the respondent had failed to do so and, hence, the provisions of section 171 had been contravened by the respondent in as much as the additional benefit of ITC at the rate of 3.04 per cent of the base price received by the respondent during the period 1-7-2017 to 31-8-2018 and the amount outstanding as on 31-8-2018, had not been passed on to the applicants and the other recipients.

An application was filed before the Standing Committee on Anti-profiteering by the applicant alleging profiteering by the respondent in respect of purchase of a flat in the respondent's project "East Crest" in Bangalore. The applicant alleged that the respondent had charged 12 per cent GST on 2/3rd of the agreement value and 12 per cent GST on the additional charges on which there was no Service Tax prior to GST and that the benefit of Input Tax Credit (ITC) had not been passed on to him by the respondent by way of commensurate reduction in price of the flat after implementation of GST with effect from 1-7-2017.

The DGAP submitted that the respondent had suo motu accepted that he did not pass on the benefit of ITC to his customers but was willing to give an undertaking that at the end of the project, he would arrive at the ITC benefit to be passed on. The DGAP, however, had claimed that the profiteering if any, has to be established at a given point of time in terms of Rule 129(6) of the CGST Rules, 2017. Accordingly, taking into consideration the benefit of ITC available in the pre-GST period in comparison to the post GST period the Report had arrived at the ITC ratio based on the taxable turnover.

The Report further submitted that the ITC as a percentage of the total turnover that was available to the respondent during the pre-GST period (April, 2016 to June, 2017) was 3.06 per cent and during the post-GST period (July, 2017 to June, 2018), it was 4.51 per cent, which confirmed that post-GST the Respondent had benefited from additional ITC to the tune of 1.45 per cent [4.51 per cent (-) 3.06 per cent] of the taxable turnover. Accordingly, the profiteered amount had been computed by comparing the applicable tax rate and the ITC available for the pre-GST period when Service Tax at the rate of 6 per cent and VAT at the rate of 4 per cent was payable with the post-GST period when the effective GST rate was 12 per cent.

The Report further submitted that the additional ITC of 1.45 per cent of the taxable turnover should have resulted in commensurate reduction in the base price. Therefore, in terms of section 171, the benefit of the additional ITC that had accrued to the respondent, was required to be passed on to the recipients. Though the respondent had not contested that any such benefit would eventually have to be passed on to the recipients at the time of giving possession of the flats, it was a fact that this had not been done so far. Thus, the payments being received from the applicant and other recipients did not take into account the benefit available to the respondent, which implied that he had retained the benefit accruing on account of the ITC. In other words, by not reducing the pre-GST base price by 1.45 per cent on account of additional benefit of ITC and charging GST at the rate of 12 per cent on the pre-GST base price, the respondent had contravened the provisions of section 171.

Based on the ITC available pre and post-GST and the details of the amount collected by the respondent from the applicant and other home buyers during the period 1-7-2017 to 30-6-2018, the DGAP had arrived at an amount of Rs. 19,69,991 the benefit of which has not been passed on by the respondent to the recipients, which included 12 per cent GST on the base profiteered amount of Rs.17,58,921 which pertained to only 51 home buyers.

Ruling

The supply of services by the applicant of transfer by way of lease of vacant plots to NMMC and PMC for use as Indoor Recreation Centre , Slaughter house and PMC Ward Office(s) will be covered under Sl. No. 3 of the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and exempt from GST.

?The supply of services by the applicant of transfer by way of lease of vacant plots to PMC for use as PMC Commissioner's residence and PMC Mayor's residence will be taxable at rate of 18 per cent under Heading No. 9972, i.e., Sl. No. 16, clause (iii) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 6]

Development Authority satisfies both the conditions and hence is considered as a Government Entity within the meaning of the Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 11.9]

Regarding the second question, whether the services provided by the main contractor are covered under clauses (a), (b) or (c) of the entry No.3(vi) of the said Notification, the following are noticed:[Para 11.10] The applicant is constructing a Housing Project at two places in around Bangalore on subcontract basis rewarded from GIEPL. The Bangalore Development Authority in its tender has stated that it has taken up construction of housing in and around Bangalore City as designed by the Government of Karnataka. Since this is a residential project for general public, the same is not covered under clause (b) or (c). [Para 11.10.1]

The projects of the applicant are involving the supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and hence is a 'works contract' within the meaning of section 2(119) of CGST Act. This works contract is for a construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, the works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and hence it is covered under clause (a) of the entry 3(vi) of the Notification, subject to the conditions. [Para 11.10.2]

Regarding the issue as to whether the recipient has procured the said services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the State Government, it is observed that the Bangalore Development Authority Act, which is passed by the State Legislature, has entrusted the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith to the BDA and the Authority has to obtain the sanction of the Government of Karnataka for every scheme they propose to implement. Hence, the condition is also satisfied. [Para 11.10.3]

Hence for the reasons stated above, the services provided by GIEPL to Bangalore Development Authority in relation to the construction of housing complexes are covered under clause (a) of entry no.3(vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended from time to time. [Para 11.10.4]

The applicant has entered into subcontract agreement with the main contractor and this is in relation to the activity covered under entry No 3(vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. As explained earlier, Bengaluru Development Authority is a Government Authority and the main contractor is providing services specified in item (vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and hence the subcontract work of works contract provided by the applicant as a subcontractor to the main contractor is covered under item (ix) of entry 3 of the said Notification as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and is taxable at 6 per cent under CGST Act, 2017, with effect from 25-1-2018. For the period from 1-7-2017 to 24-1-2018, the same is taxable at 9 per cent CGST. [Para 11.10.5]

Similar notifications are issued under the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and hence the activity of the applicant is liable to tax at 9 per cent KGST for the period between 1-7-2017 to 24-1-2018 and at 6 per cent from 25-1-2018. [Para 11.11]

In view of the foregoing, the following ruling is passed:

1.

The activity undertaken by the applicant as enumerated in the application is covered under section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and is a works contract services.

2.

Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Authority as per the provisions of the GST Law.

3.

The said transaction is covered under entry No 3(ix) of the notification No.11/2017- Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No.1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, and liable to tax at 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent KGST from 25-1.2018 and under entry No.3 (ii) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at 9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent KGST for the period earlier to 25-1-2018. [Para 12]

The works contract so executed by the applicant includes Sewerage disposal (Sewerage and STP) unit and construction of water works are covered vide Sl. No. (iii) (c) to the said notification and merit exemption where the applicable tax rate is 12 per cent (6 per cent under CGST & 6 per cent under OGST Act, 2017). [Pra 4.8]

Now coming to the issue of construction of Directors Bungalow and construction of staff-faculty quarters. It is seen that the applicant has been awarded construction of Directors Bungalow, 40 nos. staff quarters, 84 nos. Faculty Quarters in the IIT Campus, Bhubaneswar. It is also observed that the civil construction of residential quarters is not the primary work entrusted to IIT, Bhubaneswar. Accordingly, why the benefit of concessional rate at the rate of 12 per cent GST should be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant? The intention of the Legislature has been to allow concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of IIT, Bhubaneswar will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. Hence, construction of Directors Bungalow and construction of staff/faculty quarters is out of purview of exemption provided under Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST). [Para 4.9]

In view of the discussions foregoing, it is held that the works entrusted to the applicant by IIT, Bhubaneswar under contract/agreement dated 2-5-2016 cannot be termed as composite supply and, thus, entire work under the said contract shall not be entitled to concessional rate in terms of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. However, it is also held that the supply of goods and/or services or both which squarely fall within the ambit of scope of work entrusted to IIT, Bhubaneswar by Government of India shall be entitled for concessional rate under Sl. No. 3(vi) to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), 28-6-2017 (R). Accordingly, each and every supply under the subject contract shall be treated separately for determining the rate of tax under the CGST Act, 2017 read with the provisions of GST Tariff and respective exemption notifications. [Para 4.10]

For a works contract to be covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 the following conditions needs to be satisfied:

(a)

The recipient of services must be a Government Entity and in this case, Bangalore Development Authority;

(b)

The works contract services supplied by the applicant must be in relation to the works covered under (a), (b) or (c) of Entry 3(vi);

(c)

The recipient of such services must have procured these services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or local authority. [Para 10.6]

Bangalore Development Authority is an authority established by the State Government under the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 and it is entrusted with the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith. [Para 10.7]

The control over the entity rests with the Government of Karnataka and, hence, the Bangalore Development Authority satisfies both the conditions and, hence, is considered as a Government Entity within the meaning of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. [Para 10.8]

The applicant is constructing a Housing Project at two places in and around Bangalore. The Bangalore Development Authority in its tender has stated that it has taken up construction of housing in and around Bangalore City as designed by the Government of Karnataka. Since this is a residential project for general public, the same is not covered under clause (b) or (c) of Entry 3(vi). [Para 10.9.1]

The projects of the applicant are involving the supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and, hence, is a 'works contract' within the meaning of section 2(119) of CGST Act. This works contract is for a construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, the works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and, hence, it is covered under clause (a) of the Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification, subject to the conditions. [Para 10.9.2]

Regarding the issue as to whether the recipient has procured the said services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the State Government, it is observed that the Bangalore Development Authority Act, which is passed by the State Legislature, has entrusted the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith to the BDA and the Authority has to obtain the sanction of the Government of Karnataka for every scheme they propose to implement. Hence, the condition is also satisfied. [Para 10.9.3]

Hence the services provided by the applicant to the Bangalore Development Authority in relation to the construction of two housing complexes referred to in the application are covered under entry no. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and is liable to tax at 6 per cent under the CGST Act, 2017. Similarly, the services provided is covered under entry no. 3(vi)(a) of Notification (11/2017) No. FD 48 CSL 2017 dated 29-6-2017 (as amended) and is liable to tax at 6 per cent under the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. [Para 10.9.4]

Thus, activity undertaken by the applicant as enumerated in the application is covered under section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and is a works contract services. Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Entity as per the provisions of the GST Law. The transaction of the applicant would be a supply of works contract services covered under clause (a) of Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and not under Entry No. 3(ii) or 3(iv) or 3(v) of the said notification. [Para 11]

Since the supply in the instant case is in the form of Pure Services, Sr. No. 3 of the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 comes into play

In view of the above, pure services provided to a local authority is covered under Sr. No. 3 of the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. Lease of plots to NMMC for Indoor Recreation Centre

The NMMC proposes to set up the Indoor Recreation Centre which shall consist of a gymnasium, swimming pool and play courts, all of which facilities shall be accessible to the general public for a nominal fee. This can be considered to be a kind of a Public Amenity which is given to the citizens of the country and the public at large. Sr. No. 17 of the Twelfth Schedule under article 243W of the Constitution is with respect to 'Public amenities including street lighting, parking lots, bus stops and public conveniences'. An Indoor Recreation Centre can be considered as a kind of amenity which is given to the public by the local authority for recreation and the same would be similar to amenities provided by the Municipalities in their jurisdiction. Hence plots are leased by the applicant (a kind of pure services) to a Municipality, i.e., a local authority in relation to a function entrusted to such Municipality under article 243W of the Constitution and would be exempt as per Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Lease of plots to NMMC for Slaughter House

Sr. No. 18 of the Twelfth Schedule under article 243W of the Constitution is with respect to 'Regulation of Slaughter Houses and Tanneries'. Hence plots leased by the applicant (a kind of pure services) to a Municipality, i.e., a local authority for setting up Slaughter Houses can be perceived to be in relation to a function entrusted to such Municipality under article 243W of the Constitution (Regulation of Slaughter Houses and Tanneries) and would be exempt as per Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Lease of plots to PMC for PMC Ward Office

PMC is a Municipal Corporation, a local authority. Article 243W of the Constitution of India has endowed Municipalities with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government with respect to — (i) the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice; (ii) the performance of functions and the implementation of schemes as may be entrusted to them including those in relation to the matters listed in the Twelfth Schedule, etc. To carry out such work it is imperative that PMC must have an office/s for its staff who are employed to perform the services of PMC. The jurisdiction of all Municipalities in India including PMC consists of Wards. Ward Offices are necessary for PMC to enable the execution or performance of all of its functions including those under article 243W of the Constitution. In the absence of the establishment by way of a Ward Office, PMC would find it impossible to function. The said services would be exempt as per Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Lease of plots to PMC for PMC's Commissioner's and Mayor's residences

The applicant has mainly stated that the said residences are the places from where the PMC Commissioner as well as the Mayor function. This submission cannot be accepted. The Commissioner operates from his own office and so does the Mayor. The very fact that the applicant has submitted that the plots are for residences would mean that the same are for the personal use of the concerned officials. Construction of residence for officials cannot be considered to be a function envisaged under article 243W of the Constitution of India. The Authority does not agree with the applicant's contention that the leasing of land for construction of building for use as PMC Commissioner's and PMC Mayor's residences falls within the scope of Entry No. 2 of the Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution of India relating to 'Regulation of land-use and construction of buildings' or within the scope of any of the Entries of the Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution of India. In the application itself it is stated that MPPGCL has been established by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in the company and is also exercising full control over the activities of the said company. Thus, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST law, as it fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions laid down under notification No. 11/2017. [Para 5.4]

Now, the said Government Entity i.e. MPPGCL has been entrusted with the work of power generation in the State of Madhya Pradesh. The essential and sole work entrusted to MPPGCL by the Government of Madhya Pradesh is of electricity (power) generation. MPPGCL has awarded a works contract for construction of 599 residential quarters to the applicant. However, the civil construction of residential quarters is neither the primary work entrusted to MPPGCL nor it has any bearing on the work i.e. power generation by any means. Thus, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent GST should not be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant. The intention of the legislature has been to give concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general. Any work having direct involvement in the entrusted work i.e. power generation would merit exemption envisaged under Sr.No.3(vi)(c) of the Notification No.11/2017-CT (Rate) under CGST Act and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of MPPGCL will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. [Para 5.5]

The activity in question definitely did not have any relation to the principal work of power generation entrusted by the State Government to MPPGCL, and, thus, the works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No.11/2017-CT Rate dated 28-6-2017 and corresponding notification under MPGST Act, 2017. [Para 5.6]

Thus, the impugned activity of the applicant would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) classifiable under SAC 9954 read with Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017. [Para 5.7]
