summarise it all for better understanding :-

1.Service tax is applicable when a builder, deve-loper or promoter constructs a residential complex having at least 13 residential units for sale to other person or persons and uses the services of any other person for construction.

2.If a person builds a residential complex for himself and not for sale by using the services of any other person for construction, no service tax is payable.

3.Service tax is not payable for residential complexes having 12 residential units or less. 4.Service tax is not payable when lay out of the residential complex is not authorised by the concerned authority appointed for this purpose. Though it seems to be strange, no service tax is payable if the construction is unauthorized.

The view that in respect of unauthorized construction for which planning and lay out is not approved by appropriate authority no service tax is payable, has gain ground with the issuance of Circular F.No.B1/6/2005-TRU, dated July 27, 2005, which states residential complexes are normally constructed after obtaining approval statutory authority for their layout and reiterates that to be covered by the definition of residential complex the layout of the premises has to be approved by the appropriate authority.

5.If builder, developer or promoter himself is constructing a residential complex for sale without engaging a contractor or other service provider then no service tax is payable. Service tax is payable only when builder, developer or promoter uses the services of contractor or other service providers. If builder, promoter or deve-loper builds a residential complex with the services of his own staff and without using outside service providers then no service tax is payable.

6.Post-construction completion and finishing services such as glazing i.e. fitting of glasses of window etc., plastering, i.e., coating or covering wall etc. with plaster or like, painting i.e. white washing or coloring on surface like walls, roof, doors and windows etc., floor and wall tiling i.e. fitting tiles on floor and walls and other surface, wall covering and wall papering i.e. covering the walls and roof with paper or other material, wood and metal joinery and carpentry, construction of swimming pool, fitting of audio and sound applications and other similar services in relation to the a new or existing or old residential complex will also be covered by the levy of service tax.

7.Repair, alteration, renovation or restoration of residential complexes are also liable to service. These services in relation to new as well as existing or residential complex are taxable.

8.If the service provider is issuing a combined bill which includes the cost of goods and material also than at the option of service provider an abatement of 67 per cent is available vide Notification No.18/2005-ST, dated June 7, 2005 effective from June 16, 2005 which is the actual date of taxability of this particular service.

This abatement is for 67 per cent of the gross amount charged and it will include value of goods and material supplied or provided or used for providing the taxable service because the intention of the law is to charge the service and not the goods.

This abatement is subject to two main conditions. First that the service provider has not claimed the Cenvat credit on input or capital goods used for providing the service. Further the service provider claiming benefit of Notification No. 12/2003, dated June 20, 2003 and effective from July 1, 2003 related to exemption from service tax of value of all the taxable services to the extent of value of goods and materials sold by the service provider to the recipient of the service, is also not eligible to take the benefit of this abatement.

Further if the service is for finishing and completion service only, then also the benefit of above

abatement is not allowed. If a single contractor or service provider provides the construction service along with completion and finishing service, then the service provider can claim the abatement of 67 per cent of total amount charged subject to above two conditions.

9.The service providers can claim Cenvat credit as per the Cenvat as per the Cenvat Credit Rules, 2004 but claiming this Cenvat credit is subject to circumstances mentioned in point No.9 as mentioned above.

10.The service providers are eligible for exemption scheme for small service providers as notified by Notification No. 6/2005-ST, dated March 3, 2005 and in case of completion and finishing services it is advisable to use the services of small service providers to keep the effect of service tax

minimum on overall cost of construction of the residential complex.

11.The service is taxable from June 16, 2005 and the rate of service tax is 10.2 per cent.

In such cases, the promoter must have availed some ITC and paid tax (CGST and SGST/UTGST) on some supplies till 31-3-2019. In such case, there are two possibilities -

(a)

He has availed more ITC compared to the tax paid by him on his output supply [of which chances are high] . In such cases, he should reverse the excess ITC availed by him.

(b)

He has availed less ITC compared to the tax paid by him on his output supply [of which chances are low]. In such cases, he is entitled to get credit to the extent of less ITC availed by him.

In such cases, the promoter is required to make project wise calculations of ITC availed and ITC eligible, as prescribed in Annexure I in the case of REP (other than RREP) and in Annexure II in the case of RREP to Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28-6-2017.

He should apply in form GST DRC-20 and Commissioner can issue order in form GST DRC-21 to allow time to make payments in upto 24 monthly instalments [in my view, interest will be payable though the circular is silent on it].

SERVICE TAX ON CONSTRUCTION OF COMPLEX - A WELCOME CLARIFICATION

Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBEC) vide Circular No. 108/2 of 2009-ST, dated January 29, 2009 (F.No. 137/12/2006-CX-4) clarified about the service tax liability of builders/developers and purchasers of residential flats in a complex which is under-construction. The clarification provided by the tax administration is a welcome measure. It would not only clear the ambiguities but also act as stimulus for the urban housing sector in the present economic slowdown.

Introduction

1. Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBEC) vide Circular No. 108/2 of 2009-ST, dated January 29, 2009 (F.No. 137/12 of 2006-CX.4) clarified the service tax liability of builders/developers and purchasers of residential flats in a complex under construction.

Taxable Service

2. ‘Construction of Complex services’ was brought in the ambit of service tax by the Finance Act, 2005. As per section 65(105)( zzzh) of the Finance Act, 1994 (‘the Act’), taxable service means any service provided or to be provided to any person, by any other person, in relation to construction of complex.

Section 65(30a) of the Act reads as under :

‘construction of complex’ means

"(a )construction of a new residential complex or a part thereof; or

(b )completion and finishing services in relation to residential complex such as glazing, plastering, painting, floor and wall tiling, wall covering and wall papering, wood and metal joinery and carpentry, fencing and railing, construction of swimming pools, acoustic applications or fittings and other similar services; or

(c )repair, alteration, renovation or restoration of, or similar services in relation to, residential complex;"

Section 65(91a) reads as follows :

‘residential complex’ means any complex comprising of—

"(i )a building or buildings, having more than twelve residential units;

(ii )a common area; and

(iii )any one or more of facilities or services such as park, lift, parking space, community hall, common water supply or effluent treatment system,

located within a premises and the layout of such premises is approved by any authority under any law for the time being in force, but does not include a complex which is constructed by a person directly engaging any other person for designing or planning of the layout, and the construction of such complex is intended for personal use as residence by such person.

Explanation.—For the removal of doubts, it is hereby declared that for the purposes of this clause,—

(a )‘personal use’ includes permitting the complex for use as residence by another person on rent or without consideration;

(b )‘residential unit’ means a single house or a single apartment intended for use as a place of residence;"

Service tax Applicability

3. As per the Central Board of Excise & Customs vide Circular No. 96/7 of 2007 (Reference Code: 079.01), dated August 23, 2007, the promoters/developers engaged in the building construction normally should carry out their activities either—

(a)by entering into a contract with one or more independent contractor(s) for execution of the entire construction, or

(b)with the help of a person directly engaging any other person for designing or planning of the layout.

In case of the former (a) the sub-contractor(s) are liable for payment of service tax and in later (b) case, there is no service tax leviable.

If no other person is engaged for construction work and the builder/promoter/developer/any such person undertakes construction work on his own without engaging the services of any other person, then in such cases,

(i)service provider and service recipient relationship does not exist,

(ii)services provided are in the nature of self-supply of services.

In the absence of service provider and service recipient relationship, if the service provided is in the nature of self-supply of service, the question of providing taxable service to any person by any other person does not arise. Thus, no service tax on construction of residential flat is levied if the builder has constructed the flats on his own.

The necessary condition, however, remains that the promoter/developer continues to be the owner of the complex and in the event of selling, he becomes the service provider and is liable to pay service tax.

Builders/buyers’ concern

In Olety Landmark Apartment Owner's Association, In re [2021] 125 taxmann.com 381 (AAR - Karnataka), it has been held that amounts collected by resident welfare association (RWA) towards Sinking Fund meant for future supply of services to members are covered under SAC 9995 as 'Services of Membership Association' and are taxable to GST @ 18% in terms of Sl. No. 33 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. These amounts are liable to GST as they are advances towards future supply of services but not deposits.

GST is payable on non-refundable corpus fund received from members as it is advance for provision of common area maintenance services - Prinsep Association of Apartment Owners In re (2024) 17 Centax 407 = 161 taxmann.com 722 = 87 GSTL 440 (AAAR-WB) - confirming Prinsep Association of Apartment Owners In re (2024) 21 Centax 259 = 89 GSTL 295 (AAR-WB) - same view in Crimson Dawn Apartment Owners Welfare Association, In re [2025] 175 taxmann.com 16 (AAR - TN).

There are some slightly contrary views also. No service is involved. Hence, there is no GST on corpus/sinking fund collected from members. However, if these funds are utilised for supply of services, GST will be payable - same view in Vaishnavi Splendour Home Owners Welfare Association In re (2020) 80 GST 256 = 110 taxmann.com 249 (AAR-Karnataka).

The contract of the applicant with the main contractor should satisfy the following conditions to get covered under Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017:

(a)

The contract must be a composite supply of works contract.

(b)

The works must be a construction, erection, commissiong or installation of original works.

(c)

It must pertain to Railways. [Para 4.4]

In the instant case, the contract is for supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates and involves excavation of pits, casting and plastering and other parts which involve construction, erection, commissioning and installation of original works. Hence the second condition is satisfied.

As the contract is related to an immovable property, the entire contract is covered under the definition of works contract under section 2(119). Hence the first condition is also satisfied. [Para 4.5]

The main issue is whether this is a contract pertaining to Railways. The main contractor has obtained the contract from Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited and then subcontracted to the applicant. The work is related to supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates as per the requirement of DFCCIL. [Para 4.6]

Since the works related to railways network, the contract can be said to be pertaining to Railways. The term pertaining to Railways is more expansive and includes other establishments other than Indian Railways. Hence the contract is pertaining to Railways. [Para 4.8]

There is no stipulation in Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 that the contract must be executed to the Railways, but it is sufficient that it must be pertaining to Railways and the supplier and the recipient in each of the contract is immaterial. [Para 4.9]

Hence the subcontract work is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017) and is liable to tax at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST or 12 per cent IGST) with effect from 22-8-2017. [Para 4.10]

Ruling

The contract work of the applicant to the main contractor, who is executing the works contract to DFFCCIL, is liable to tax at 6 per cent under CGST Act and at 6 per cent under Karnataka GST Act or 12 per cent under IGST Act, 2017. The relevant entry is Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017).

The date of application of the rate of tax of 12 per cent is from 22-8-2017. [Para 5]

I am planning to construct a residential complex with more than twelve houses. I plan to give them on rent to various persons. I have given contract to a contractor to build the complex for me. Should the contractor charge service tax from me? The service of residential complex is not taxable if the residential complex is intended for personal use as residence. As per Explanation ( a) to section 65(91a ), ‘personal use’ includes permitting the complex for use as residence by another person on rent or without consideration. Thus, in your case, the service is not taxable.

The question will arise if you after some time, decide to sell the flats instead of giving these on rent. In such case, the service tax cannot be levied, as what is important is the nature of service at the time of providing service. Subsequent events cannot change the nature of service provided, particularly when the words used are ‘intended for personal use’ and not ‘used for personal residence’.

When construction of residential complex services can be treated as ‘export of service’ for exemption of service tax ?

In case of construction of residential complex services, the service will be ‘export of service’ only if - (a) the immovable property is situated abroad, (b) the service is delivered outside India and used in business or for any other purpose outside India and (c) payment for such service is received in convertible, i.e., free foreign exchange.

What is the value for purpose of calculation of service tax?

Service tax is payable on gross amount charged for service provided or to be provided.

Often contract for construction of complex is a compo-site contract, i.e., inclusive of material cost. In such cases, instead of identifying value of taxable services in a composite contract, tax on service of construction of residential complex can be paid on 33 per cent of gross amount charged. This would be so if (a) the gross amount charged includes value of goods and materials supplied or provided or used by provider of the construction service for providing such service and (b) Cenvat credit of inputs and capital goods is not availed. This simple method is not available in case of only completion and finishing services (Notification No. 18/2005-ST dated June 7, 2005).

Is there a simple method to pay service tax?

A service provider providing taxable service of construction of residential complex can opt to pay service tax on 33 per cent of gross amount charged. The gross amount should include value of goods and materials supplied or provided or used. However, he can avail this concession only if - (a) He does not avail Cenvat of duty paid on inputs and capital goods (He can avail Cenvat of input services) and (b) He does not avail benefit of Notification No. 12/2003-ST dated June 20, 2003 and Notification No. 18/2005-ST dated June 7, 2005.

This simple method is not available in case the service provider provides only completion and finishing services (as in such cases, material content will be much less).

The partial exemption is available only if the gross amount charged includes value of goods and materials supplied or provided or used by provider of the commercial or industrial construction service for providing such service [Explanation to Notification No. 18/2005-ST]. Thus, if the customer provides some material, its value will have to be added for purpose of payment of service tax.

As per Notification No. 12/2003-ST, no service tax is payable on value of material or goods sold to recipient of service. Thus, if a service provider avails exemption under 15/2004-ST, he cannot avail concessional rate of 33 per cent of gross amount charged to customers.

The service provider can have benefit either under No. 12/2003-ST or No. 15/2004-ST and not both.

Notification No. 17/2005 - Soft treatment for Infrastructure development services

4. Infrastructure Development has been given a soft treatment by tax authorities in India with a variety of exemptions and rebates. The Service Tax Department has decided to join the bandwagon. Notification No. 17/2005 exempts works related to site formation and clearance, excavation and earthmoving and such other similar activities provided to any person by any other person in the course of construction of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels, dams, ports or other ports. The important thing to note in this Notification is that the insistence on a commercial concern providing the service - a regular feature of other notifications on Service Tax - is not there.

8. Notification No. 22/2005 exempts services provided by a non-resident in the course of sailing of a ship. However, the Notification is fraught with riders:

uThe service should be provided outside India and consumed outside India

uThe ship should be

(i )registered as an Indian ship under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 (44 of 1958);

(ii )registered under the Coasting Vessels Act, 1838 (19 of 1838);

(iii )registered under the Inland Vessels Act, 1917 (1 of 1917); or

(iv )chartered and licenced under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958

uThe ship should be owned or chartered by

(i )a citizen of India;

(ii )a company or a body established by or under any Central Act or State Act which has its principal place of business in India; or

(iii )a co-operative society which is registered or deemed to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912 (2 of 1912), or any other law relating to co-operative societies for the time being in force in any State,

uThe exemption is available only if the taxable services are provided in relation to

(i )handling of ships in a port outside India;

(ii )handling or storage of goods carried in a ship in a port outside India; or

(iii )any other services related to the handling of ships or goods carried in a ship.

Explanation.—For the purposes of this notification, ‘non-resident person’ means a person, who has established a business or has a fixed establishment from which the service is provided or to be provided, or has his permanent address or usual place of residence, in a country other than India.

The appellant had entered into agreement with IIT, Bhubaneswar for Project Management Consultancy (PMC) works. It sought advance ruling on whether the nature of supply made by appellant to IIT, Bhubaneswar vide the agreement dated 2-5-2016 is a work contract services under Central Goods and Services Tax Act (Odisha State Goods and Services Tax Act) relying on clause 119 to section 2 read with item no. 6(a) to the schedule-II. For that matter, the applicable rate of tax would be governed by Sr. No. 3 (classification code 9954) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and whether on the basis of law as well as fact, IIT, Bhubaneswar is a 'Governmental Authority' or a 'Government Entity' as defined in clause nos. (ix) and (x) in the explanation at serial no. 4 to Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (rate), dated 28-6-2017 Central GST Act and what would be applicable rate of GST.

It is also sought ruling on whether the construction services related to sewerage project falls under clause (iii) of serial no. 3 (Classification Code 9954) of the table in the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

AAR by order held that where Government of India, Ministry of Human Resource Development is exercising full control over activities of IITs all over country, IIT, Bhubaneswar qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for purpose of GST law, however mere fact that number of works are entrusted by IIT Bhubaneswar to applicant under a single contract/agreement, would not make it entitled to be categorised as 'composite supply', and, thus, entire work under said contract shall not be entitled to concessional rate in terms of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

RAJESH DHAWAN*

Whether charges collected by Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) towards marketing fee fall under ‘Technical inspection and certification services’ ?

Yes. In the case of Grasim Industries Ltd. v. CCE [2009] 21 STT 128 (Chennai - CESTAT), the Tribunal held that charges collected by BIS towards marketing fee are part and parcel of the cost of the services rendered by the agency and, therefore, marketing fee charged by BIS is includible in the value of taxable service and subject to service tax.

Whether lease rental falls under ‘Airport services’ ?

No. The Government in its Circular No. 80/10/2004-ST, dated 17-9-2004 has clarified that in case a part of airport/civil enclave premises is rented/leased out, the rental/lease charges would not be subjected to service tax, as the activity of letting out premises does not amount to rendering a service under the category of ‘Airport services’. With effect from 1-6-2007, service tax has been levied on renting of immovable property for commercial purpose and same falls under ‘Renting of immovable property services’.

Whether advertising service falls under ‘Business exhibition services’ ?

No. The Government in its Circular No. 80/10/2004-ST, dated 17-9-2004 has clarified that while services rendered in relation to a circular, label, documents, hoardings or any other audio visual representation of a product or service fall under ‘Advertisement services’, the services relating to actual exhibition or display of product or services would fall under the category of ‘Business exhibition services’.

Whether construction of road in commercial complex falls under ‘Commercial or industrial construction services’ ?

Yes. The Government in Instruction No. vide TRU’s letter F.No. B1/6/2005-TRU, dated 27-7-2005 has clarified that if the contract for construction of commercial complex is a single contract and the construction of road is not recognised as a separate activity as per the contract, then service tax would be leviable on the gross amount charged for construction including the value of construction of roads.

Whether services provided by IRCTC in trains fall under ‘Outdoor caterer services’ ?

Yes. In the Shatabadi/Rajdhani trains, the IRCTC-licensed private contractors (known as sub-licencees) provide catering services to passangers on boarding the trains and the private contractor pays service tax under the outdoor catering service classifiable under section 65(105)(zzt ) of the Finance Act, 1994 for the catering services provided. The Government in its letter, F. No. 332/38/2006-TRU, dated 1-8-2006, has clarified that "in view of the definition of ‘outdoor catering service’ under section 65(105)( zzt), outdoor caterer under section 65(76a) and caterer under section 65(24) and, the service provided by IRCTC appear to be classifiable under ‘Outdoor catering services’."

In the case of SAJ Flight Services (P.) Ltd. v. Superintendent of Central Excise [2006] 3 STT 165 (Ker.), the Court held that supply of foods and beverages to aircrafts for service to the passengers on board will attract service tax under ‘Catering services’.

Whether service provided by club or trade association to its member falls under ‘Services by club or association’ ?

Yes. The Board in the Instruction No. 137/50/2008-CX.4, dated 5-3-2008 has clarified that the services provided by club to its own members, or to the guest of the members are subject to service tax under the ‘Club or association services’ and the plea that they are providing the service to their own member, is not sustainable.

Whether repair, renovation, etc., of old residential complex falls under ‘Construction of residential complex services’ ?

Yes. The definition of ‘Construction of complex’ includes repair, alteration, renovation or restoration of, or similar services in relation to, residential complex. The Government in its departmental instructions vide TRU’s letter F. No. B1/6/2005-TRU, dated 2-7-2005 has clarified that ‘such services provided in relation to residential complexes which are in existence before the levy has come into force and are not new, would also be liable to be taxed’.

Whether maintenance & repair of ATM falls under ‘ATM operations, maintenance or management services’ ?

Exemptions to certain construction activities

Though construction activity is declared service, various exemptions are available. These are summarised below.

Non commercial construction related services provided to Government or local authority or governmental authority is exempt - Services provided to the Government or local authority or governmental authority are exempt from service tax vide Sr No.12 of Notification No. 25/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 [see under Government Related Services' in another chapter for details].

Construction of Pipelines for water supply for Government Board is not commercial construction - Construction of Pipelines for water supply for Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board (GWSSB) is not commercial construction, even if some charge is made for water supply and supply of water is part of duties and functions of State - Dinesh Chandra Agarwal Infracon v. CCE (2011) 30 STT 75 (CESTAT) * Larsen and Toubro Ltd. v. CST (2011) 9 taxmann.com 325 = 31 STT 12 = 38 VST 312 (CESTAT) * Nagarjuna Construction Co. v. CCE (2011) 38 VST 303 (CESTAT).

The decisions were followed in IVRCL Infrastructures v. CST (2011) 32 STT 118 = 12 taxmann.com 13 (CESTAT) while granting stay.

Civil structure relating to rehabilitation of slum dweller - Construction of a civil structure or any other original works pertaining to the "In-situ rehabilitation of existing slum dwellers using land as a resource through private participation" under the Housing for All (Urban) Mission/Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, only for existing slum dwellers is exempt from service tax - Sr No.13(ba) of Notification No. 25/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 inserted w.e.f. 1-4-2016.

Construction under specified housing schemes - Construction of a civil structure or any other original works pertaining to the "Beneficiary-led individual house construction/enhancement" under the Housing for All (Urban) Mission/Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana is exempt from service tax - Sr No.13(bb) of Notification No. 25/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 inserted w.e.f. 1-4-2016.

Low cost housing schemes - Construction service of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house in a housing project approved by the competent authority under: (i) the "Affordable Housing in Partnership" component of the Housing for All (Urban) Mission/Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (ii) any housing scheme of a State Government is exempt from service tax - Sr No.14(ca) of Notification No. 25/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 inserted w.e.f. 1-4-2016.

Construction of single residential unit other that part of a complex is exempt - Services by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to single residential unit other than as a part of a residential complex are exempt - Sr No. 14(b) of Notification No. 25/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 (see above for definition of 'original work').

Thus, if a single residential unit is a part of residential complex, it will not be exempt from service tax.

Residential Complex - "Residential complex" means any complex comprising of a building or buildings, having more than one single residential unit [see definition clause 2(zc) of Notification No. 25/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 effective from 1-7-2012].

Till 1-7-2012, a construction was coming within the definition of 'residential complex' only if it contained more than 12 residential units [section 65(91a) as existing upto 1-7-2012].

Single Residential Unit - "Single residential unit" means a self-contained residential unit which is designed for use, wholly or principally, for residential purposes for one family [see definition clause 2(ze) of Notification No. 25/2012-ST].

From the above work details submitted by the applicant it is very clear that the entire contact is in the form of a composite contract consisting of supply of goods and services and where the main intention is to provide drinking water to the villages after removing excess Iron impurities and which therefore would be the main part of the contract. Here it would not be out of place to mention that the applicant is claiming that the work performed by them are 'water treatment schemes' and not 'water purification schemes'. In their submissions they have mentioned that when Extracting water from tube well, passing it through treatment plant of removing unwanted contaminants like Iron from ground water and eventually lifting it to overhead tank (in short the scheme). These works would be covered under Sr. No. 3, Column 3 (iii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. In view of the above discussions and also in view of the submissions made by the applicant, the work done by them is a composite supply which attracts the provisions of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. The said Notifications has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in Column 3 of the Table in the said Notfn, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein. Based on the above discussions, the relevant clause applicable to the subject case would be clauses (iii) of the said Notfn, as amended by Notfn No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-10-2017. A plain reading of Sr. No. 3, clause (iii) reveals that 'composite supply of WCS supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of, pipeline, conduit or plant for (i) water supply (ii) water treatment, or (iii) sewerage treatment or disposal attracts a tax rate of 6 per cent each of CGST and SGST. However, the benefit of 12 per cent tax rate would be available to the applicant only if the Works Contract services provided by them are Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of, pipeline, conduit or plant for (i) water supply (ii) water treatment. [Para 5]

In view of the extensive deliberations as held hereinabove TSH 9954 is applicable to the subject contract of extracting water from tube well, passing it through treatment plant of removing unwanted contaminants like iron from ground water and eventually lifting it to overhead tank and the same would attract a tax rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST and SGST). 23.9-1 Charges of PLC, EDC , parking space charges etc. are part of 'construction service' -for valuation of apartment A builder/contractor charges separately for Preferential Location Charges (PLC), additional charges for modifications suggested by customers, maintenance during construction period, covered parking charges, EDC (External Development Charges), IDC (Internal Development Charges) etc. In my view, all these are 'naturally bundled services. These should get covered under 'construction of complex' and be eligible for abatement in valuation - view confirmed in FAQ (Part II) No. 4 issued by CBI&C vide circular F No. 354/32/2019-TRU dated 14-5-2019.

Preferential location service is naturally bundled with construction of residential complex and GST rate is same as that of main service - Shreno Ltd. v. CCE (2021) 54 GSTL 187 (CESTAT) - same view in CBIC Circular No. 234/28/2024-GST dated 11-10-2024.

External development and infrastructure development charges are part of value of construction services - Ashiana Housing Ltd. In re (2022) 91 GST 577 = 138 taxmann.com 92 (AAAR-Haryana).

Preferential location charges is part of value of land - Location charges or preferential location charges (PLC) paid upfront in addition to the lease premium for long term lease of land constitute part of upfront amount charged for long term lease of land and are eligible for the same tax treatment - para 10 of CBIC Circular No. 177/09/2022-TRU dated 3-8-2022. [principle for lease of land but applies but here also].

Preferential location service is naturally bundled with construction of residential complex and GST rate is same as that of main service - Shreno Ltd. v. CCE (2021) 54 GSTL 187 (CESTAT).

Common amenities are part of principal supply - Common amenities (like club house, swimming pool), water, electricity, drainage, sewage, society formation, legal services and documentation charges are for services which are integral part of composite supply of works contract, construction services being principal supply. These are 'naturally bundled'. However, advance maintenance charges, stamp duty, corpus fund and share application money will not be included in value of apartment - Joyville Shapoorji Housing P Ltd. In re (2020) 81 GST 559 = 113 taxmann.com 369 (AAR-Maharashtra).

Club Membership fees not part of construction service - Club membership fee cannot be part of construction service and should not get covered under 'naturally bundled service'. Similarly, maintenance service provided after construction is over is not part of 'construction service' and should not be eligible for abatement.

Service of access to club house and common amenities is considered as a supply and proportionate cost should be includible in value of service - Godrej Properties Ltd. In re (2023) 8 Centax 35 (AAR- Kar).

Contrary decision of AAAR in respect of PLC - In Bengal Peerless Housing Development Company Ltd., In re [2019] 110 taxmann.com 34 (AAAR-WB), it has been held that plc and car parking space charges are separate service charged separately at the option of customer. These are not part of value of construction service and no abatement is available in respect of PLC or car parking space charged [In other words, it is not composite supply]. The decision in Bengal Peerless Housing Development Co. Ltd. In re [2019] 105 taxmann.com 58 (AAR-West Bengal) has been reversed, where, it was held that service of construction of a dwelling unit in a residential complex, bundled with services relating to the preferential location of the unit and right to use car parking space and common areas and facilities, is a composite supply, construction service being the principle supply. Entire value of the composite supply is, therefore, to be treated, for the purpose of taxation, as supply of construction service. [In my view, decision of AAR is correct. Reversal of that decision by AAAR is incorrect].

Contrary decision in case of sale of parking space - In Eden Real Estates P Ltd. In re (2023) 146 taxmann.com 459 = 71 GSTL 327 = 2 Centax 287 = 96 GST 547 (AAR-WB), it has been held that supply of service of right to use car parking space would be taxable @ 18%. The reason given that this was at the option of customer and hence is not naturally bundled with construction service - view confirmed in Eden Real Estates (P.) Ltd., In re [2023] 150 taxmann.com 517 = 98 GST 687 = 74 GSTL 451 = 6 Centax 211 (AAAR-WB).

In respect of development rights or FSI transferred or payment of upfront amount for long term lease of land on or after 1-4-2019 proposed to be used for residential apartments, GST is not payable on TDR, FSI or payment of upfront amount for long term lease of land if residential apartment is sold before completion. However, if some residential apartments remain unsold on date of completion, proportionate GST is payable on TDR, FSI or long term lease of land by promoter under reverse charge.

In case of commercial apartments, GST is payable on development rights or FSI transferred or payment of upfront amount for long term lease of land after 1-4-2019, whether or not commercial apartments are sold before obtaining completion certificate. Where promoter opts to pay tax at full rate (8%/12%) after availing ITC, proportionate reversal of Input Tax Credit is required in respect of apartments remaining unsold as on date of completion or first occupation, whichever is earlier.

The reversal is required to be made on date of completion of project. Reversal should be as per rule 42 of CGST Rules in respect of inputs and input services and rule 43 of CGST Rules in respect of capital goods.

Question No. 36: Can a developer take deduction of actual value of land involved in sale of unit instead of taking deduction of deemed value of land as per Paragraph 2 to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017? Ans: No. Valuation mechanism prescribed in paragraph 2 of the notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 clearly prescribes one-third abatement towards value of land.

Therefore, the value of land or undivided share of land is deemed to be one-third of the total amount charged for the supply irrespective of the actual value of land and accordingly the applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of the total amount charged for the supply in arriving at the taxable value of the supply. [Para 11]

The next question raised by the applicant is whether the activity of purchase of land, development of the same into plots and sale of the same to various customers without collecting any advance from the customers for undertaking the development activities attract GST. The contention of the applicant is that the activity is sale of land and it is neither a supply of goods nor a supply of services as per Schedule III of the CGST Act. As per Paragraph 5(b) of Schedule II of the CGST Act construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly, except where the entire consideration has been received after issuance of completion certificate, where required by the competent authority or after its first occupation, whichever is earlier shall be treated as a supply of services. In the instant case, it is stated by the applicant that it is not receiving any advance from its customers for undertaking development activities in the plot and the plot is sold after development. Hence the transaction is in respect of sale of developed plots/land and is covered by Paragraph 5 of Schedule III of the CGST Act which stipulates that sale of land and, subject to clause (b) of paragraph 5 of Schedule II, sale of building shall be treated neither as a supply of goods nor a supply of service. Therefore, the transaction is not liable to GST. [Para 12]

Abatement scheme of 30% for payment of service tax if value includes value of land

Service provider can opt to pay service tax on value of services. However, if he is unable to compute the value of services, he can pay service tax under composition scheme. The builder or developer is undertaking construction of commercial or residential unit, he can pay service tax on 30% of value if the value includes land value - Sr No. 12 of Notification No. 26/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 as amended w.e.f. 1-4-2016.

Till 1-4-2016, the service tax payable was on 25% or 30% of value as follows - (a) If carpet area of residential complex is upto 2,000 square feet and amount charged is less than Rs one crore - 25% (b) If carpet area of residential complex is 2,000 square feet or more or amount charged is Rs one crore or more - 30% (c) commercial construction - 30% [amendment w.e.f. 1-3-2013 and as existing upto 1-4-2016].

Till 1-3-2013, the rate applicable was 25% in all above cases].

The service provider can avail Cenvat credit of input services and capital goods but not of duty paid on input goods - Sr No. 12 of Notification No. 26/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012, effective from 1-7-2012.

Service tax payable even if part consideration received before obtaining completion certificate - In case of construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, intended for a sale to a buyer, wholly or partly except where entire consideration is received after issuance of completion certificate by the competent authority, service tax can be paid on 25%/30% of amount charged, if the value of land is included in the amount charged from the service provider.

Amount to include fair market value of material supplied by service receiver - The amount charged shall be the sum total of the amount charged for the service including the fair market value of all goods and services supplied by the recipient(s) in or in relation to the service, whether or not supplied under the same contract or any other contract. From the fair market value, following can be deduced - (i) the amount charged for such goods or services supplied to the service provider, if any; and (ii) the value added tax or sales tax, if any, levied thereon. The fair market value of goods and services so supplied may be determined in accordance with the generally accepted accounting principles.

Thus, if the customer has supplied some material by charging for the same, its amount can be deducted including Vat/Sales tax.

For example, fair market value of material supplied by service receiver is Rs. one lakh and the service receiver, instead of supplying the material free, has charged the service provider Rs. 60,000 plus Rs. 3,000 as Vat, Rs. one lakh will be added to the amount charged by service provider and deduction of Rs. 63,000 will be given. In effect, Rs. 37,000 will be added.

The provision of adding value of free supplied material to contractor (service provider) has been held invalid in Bhayana Builders v. CST (2013) 42 GST 76 = 38 taxmann.com 221 (CESTAT LB). In my view, this decision cannot apply in respect of services provided after 1-7-2012. See discussions under Works Contract Service.

Inclusions/exclusions of other amounts collected by builder/developer from customer - Preferential Location Charges (PLC), additional charges for modifications suggested by customers, maintenance during construction period, covered parking charges etc. These are naturally bundled services and should get covered under construction of complex' and be eligible for abatement in valuation.

The builder collects some charges like External Development Charges etc. which are payable to Government authorities. However, this is actually liability of builder himself. He does not act as pure agent of the customer. These should be includible in value of service but should be eligible for abatement.

However, club membership fee is not part of construction service and cannot get covered under 'naturally bundled service'. Similarly, maintenance service provided after construction is over is not part of construction service and should not be eligible for abatement.

If the builder/developer collects some amounts on actual basis, such as deposits for some activities like society membership, electricity deposit and connection charges for handing over to concerned authorities, it can be said that he is acting as pure agent of the customer and these are not includible in value.

Service of public transport by vessel - Public transport, other than predominantly for tourism purpose, in a vessel between places located in India - Sr. No. 17(d) of Notification Nos. 12/2017-CT (Rates) and 9/2017-IT (Rates) both dated 28-6-2017, effective from 1-7-2017. No GST on tickets of private ferry used for passenger transportation - Private ferries are used as means of transport from one island to another in Andaman and Nicobar Islands [In fact, used in many other places like Howrah also]. - Exemption as per Sl. No 17(d) of notification No. 12/2017- CT (Rate) dated 28.06.2017 is for "transportation of passengers by public transport, other than predominantly for tourism purpose, in a vessel between places located in India". - - This exemption would apply to tickets purchased for transportation from one point to another irrespective of whether the ferry is owned or operated by a private sector enterprise or by a PSU/government. The expression 'public transport' used in the exemption notification only means that the transport should be open to public. Transportation by water for tourism purposes taxable - Transportation by water which is predominantly for tourism, such as services which may combine with transportation, sightseeing, food and beverages, music, accommodation such as in shikara, cruise etc. would be taxable - para 18 of CBIC Circular No. 177/09/2022-TRU dated 3-8-2022.

26.5 Transport of passengers by air

Air transport services falls under group 99642.

In following cases, the rate is 5% (2.5% CGST and 2.5% SGST) or 5% IGST - (a) economy class (b) embarking from or terminating in regional connectivity scheme airport. ITC of service is available but not of goods.

Transport of passengers by air in other than economy class is 18% w.e.f. 22-9-2025 - Sr No. 8(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 8/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017 as. There is no restriction on availment of input tax credit. Earlier, the GST rate was 12%.

Transport of passengers in helicopter on seat sharing basis taxable @ 5% w.e.f. 1-7-2017 - Service of transportation of passengers, with or without accompanied baggage, by air, in a helicopter on seat share basis is taxable @ 5% (2.5% CGST and 2.5% SGST) or 5% IGST, if credit of input tax charged on goods used in supplying the service has not been taken - Sr No. 8(ivb) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 8/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017 as inserted w.e.f. 10-10-2024.

As recommended by the 54th GST Council, payment of GST on transportation of passengers, with or without accompanied baggage, by air, in a helicopter on seat share basis is hereby regularized on 'as is where is' basis for the period from 01.07.2017 to 09.10.2024 [but no refund will be admissible] - CBIC Circular No. 234/28/2024-GST dated 11-10-2024.

'As is' means if tax was not paid earlier, it will not be payable now for that period. of goods or services or both to SEZ unit or SEZ Developer is inter-State supply. This is a specific provision and hence will prevail over general provision as contained in section 12(3)(c) of IGST Act, which states that in case of supply of short term accommodation or event management services, place of supply is where immovable property is located. Hence, in case of supply of such services, IGST will be payable and not CGST and SGST/UTGST. Further, if such supply is for operations, these will be zero rated supplies. These can be made under LUT/bond without payment of GST or on payment of IGST. If such supply is for authorised operations, IGST will be refunded if paid or input tax credit refund can be obtained if supplied under LUT/Bond. Endorsement of specified officer of SEZ will be required that these services are for authorised operations - CBI&C circular No. 48/22/2018-GST dated 14-6-2018.

Accommodation services in hotels rendered to SEZ unit is zero rated, LUT should be executed - Accommodation service proposed to be rendered by applicant to SEZ units were covered under IGST as it was an inter-State supply as per section 7(5)(b) of IGST Act, 2017 and same could be treated as zero rated supplies and invoice could be raised without charging Tax after executing LUT under section 16 - Carnation Hotels (P.) Ltd., In re [2019] 110 taxmann.com 196 (AAR - Karnataka)

However, in a contrary decision, in Gogte Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd., In re (2018) 68 GST 20 = 93 taxmann.com 201 (AAR - Kar), it has been held that in case of accommodation services supplied to employees and guests of SEZ units outside the SEZ are taxable to CGST and SGST (of State where the hotel is located).

25.3-6 Accommodation service with food, housekeeping, TV, Internet, parking is composite supply

Accommodation service with food, housekeeping, TV, Internet, parking is 'composite supply', with accommodation is principal supply. The service falls under heading 996311. If total amount charges is less than Rs. 1,000 per day, it is exempt - Srisai Luxurious Stay LLP In re (2020) 81 GST 372 = 116 taxmann.com 399 = 76 GSTL 79 = 8 Centax 264 (AAR-Karn). [Now w.e.f. 18-7-2022, the service will be taxable even if amount charged less than Rs. 1,000 per day]

Value of Supply (Declared tariff upto 27-7-2018) less than Rs. 1,000 - Nil [Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 9/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017, effective from 1-7-2017 and existing upto 1-10-2019].

Value of Supply (Declared tariff upto 27-7-2018) of Rs. 7,500 or more - 28% (14% SGST/UTGST and 14% CGST)

The applicant in their submissions has stated that the Renting of Immovable Property service rendered by them as a local authority to State Govt. offices and Central Govt. offices are fully exempted. The renting of immovable property service rendered by them as a local authority to Co-operative society are not exempted but chargeable to tax Since the society and transport corporation TNSTC are covered under the definition of Government Entity only and they are not State Govt. Nationalised Banks are not Central Govt. and so the services rendered to them are not exempted but chargeable to tax. [Para 11.2]

From the Lease Agreement executed, it is seen that the applicant has leased a part of the premises owned by them to the 'The Tamil Nadu Industrial Investment Corporation Ltd.' for a monthly rent. Also, from the rental receipt copies furnished by the applicant, it is seen that the premises is leased on monthly rental basis. The nature of supply is 'Renting of immovable property' as claimed by the applicant. The issue to be decided is whether the exemption under Sl. No. 8 of the Notification No. 12/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable to such supplies.

Any service provided by Central Government, State Government, Union territory or a local authority to another Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority, which is not included in the Proviso therein, is exempted under the said entry. In the instant case, the applicant is a 'Local Authority' and therefore, the service of Renting of Immovable Property service, supplied to Central Government, State Government are exempted vide this entry. [Para 11.4]

Therefore, renting of immovable property service provided by the applicant to another Central/State Government, union territory or local authority is exempted from tax as per Sl. Normally the providers of accommodation services do provide the maintenance and security services along with the accommodation services as the entire dwelling would be under their control, but not under the control of roomer. Thus in the ordinary course of business the maintenance and security services are supplied in conjunction with each other. Thus the third condition is also fulfilled. Thus it is concluded that the impugned services of the applicant do qualify to be a composite supply. [Para 7.10] The second question is whether renting of property by applicant is covered under entry 12 of the exemption Notification 12/2017 (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. The applicant, in this regard, contended that residential dwelling has not been defined in the Act, in terms of the normal trade parlance is any residential accommodation, but does not include hotel, motel, inn, quest house, camp-site, lodge, house boat, or like places and hence they are engaged in renting of residential dwelling, not meant for temporary stay. The applicant stresses upon two factors i.e. (i) residential dwelling is given on rent for use as residence and (ii) it is rented for long term and hence claims the exemption under Sl.No.12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. The services provided by the applicant are covered under accommodation services under SAC 996311, as held in the previous paras, the exemption under Sl.No.12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is not applicable to the impugned transaction.[Para 7.11]

The third question is whether the activity of leasing of residential units for further residential leasing would qualify for exemption under entry 14 of the Exemption Notification. This question is subject to the condition that the answer to issue 2 is negative, in which case the applicant contends that they should be entitled to exemption under entry 14 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, subject to satisfaction of conditions mentioned therein, irrespective of period of stay. Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, vide Sl.No.14 exempts the Services provided by a hotel, inn, guest house, club or campsite, by whatever name called, for residential or lodging purposes, having value of supply of a unit of accommodation below or equal to one thousand rupees per day or equivalent. In the instant case the services provided by the applicant are covered under SAC 996311 as accommodation services and hence the exemption is applicable to the transaction of the applicant subject to the condition that the value of supply is less than or equal to one thousand rupees per day or equivalent. Thus the applicant is entitled for exemption under Sl.No.14 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, subject to fulfilment of the required conditions.[Para 7.12]

The last question is whether the activity of leasing of residential units for further residential leasing would qualify for exemption under entry 12 of the Exemption Notification. In the instant case, the applicant has let out residential units to commercial entities who have further let out the same for use as residence and that the Entry No. 12 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 appears to give an absolute exemption to the activity of leasing for use as residence, irrespective of the legal status of the supplier or recipient of supply; the condition of used as residence' is satisfied even in this case also and hence the activity of leasing out residential units to commercial concerns for the purpose of residential leasing should be eligible for exemption under entry 12 of the Exemption Notification; the intention behind the said exemption is to provide relief from GST on residential dwelling. Accordingly, in order for the said objective to be fulfilled both legs of the transaction (i.e., renting of property by the applicant to a business entity and further renting of the property by the entity to the Tenants for use as residence) should be covered under the exemption.[Para 7.13]

It is pertinent to mention here that the Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a transaction based tax, with seamless input tax credit at each transaction level. In the instant case two transactions are involved. The first being a transaction between the applicant and the business entity and the second between the business entity and the actual tenant. Thus the two transactions are different and the taxability/exemption of these transactions need to be examined individually. In the transaction between the applicant and business entity, the renting of residential dwelling is not for use as residence by the business entity but in the course or furtherance of the business of the said entity and hence the exemption under entry No. 12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 is not applicable to the impugned transaction. On the other hand in the transaction between the business entity and the tenant, the service amount to renting/leasing of rooming house which falls under accommodation services that get covered under SAC 996311 and hence the exemption under entry No. 12 of Notification 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 would not be applicable to the said transaction. [Para 7.14]

Collection of Room Rent for temporary stay :The applicant has stated that the activity is allowing public to use single bed room/double bed room on daily basis in the bus-stand. They have claimed that the activity is a function listed at Entry (q) of the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution. As, it can be seen, the said entry provides 'Public amenities including street lighting, parking lots, bus stops and public conveyances.' Renting room for temporary stay on daily rent basis is not an activity in relation to the activities stipulated at entry Entry (q), as it is not in the genre of the inclusive-activities specified in the said entry. But is an activity of commercial nature. Therefore, providing rooms for temporary stay in the Bus-stand is not an activity in relation to the function at Entry (q) of the Twelfth Schedule and hence, Notification No. 14/2017 -C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 said entry exempts 'services of accommodation for residential or lodging purposes, having value of supply of a unit of accommodation below or equal to one thousand rupees per day or equivalent'. In the case at hand the service is extended by the applicant and the consideration is mentioned as Rs. 40/- per day per single bed and Rs. 60/- per double bed/per day, which is well within the value of supply mentioned to be exempted under this entry. Accordingly the service of renting of room for temporary stay is exempted under Sl. No. 14 of the Notification No. 12/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended.

Providing toilets for use of Public in public places is a public amenity of Public conveniences and therefore, allowing use of toilet is an activity in relation to function at Entry (q) of the Twelfth schedule entrusted to a Municipality under article 243W. An occupancy certificate (OC), issued by the local authorities, certifies that a building is fit for occupation and has been constructed as per the approved plan and in compliance with local law.

There are 3 different certificates issued at successive short periods and these are explained below-

(i)

Completion Certificate-The concerned authorities would issue a completion certificate (CC) to a housing project, after ensuring that all requirements with regard to the project is complete so that it is suitable for habitation. It is only after a CC is issued to a project that it becomes ready for possession for home buyers.

(ii)

Occupancy Certificate- An OC, on the other hand, is a certificate stating that the project has been built in accordance with all construction norms, building bye-laws, etc. It is only after a project receives an OC, can the builder apply for various utilities for the project and.

(iii)

Possession Certificate-A possession certificate is issued to the buyer by the developer, as proof of transfer of ownership. It mentions the date of possession of the property by the new buyer. This certificate is relevant very much from the income-tax angle as it will serve as a piece of evidence for date of acquisition of the property thus fulfilling the conditions with regard to the relevant exemption provisions of the Income-tax Act (the Act).

Clause 5(b) of the Schedule II of CGST Act, 2017 stipulates that "Construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly" shall be treated as supply of service except where the entire consideration was received after issuance of completion certificate.

In other words, if any consideration is received before issuance of completion certificate involving the construction of a complex, building, civil structure intended for sale to a buyer then it will be considered as supply of a service, liable for GST and if the whole consideration is paid by the Buyer after the issuance of occupancy certificate or first occupancy, whichever is earlier, then it will be outside the GST implications i.e. no GST will be imposable.

Newtech Promoters and Developers (P.) Ltd. v. State of U.P. [Civil Appeal Nos. 6745 to 6749 of 2021 (Arising out of SLP (Civil) No(s). 37113715 OF 2021)]-Date of Judgment 11-11-2021/[2021] 132 taxmann.com 137/169 SCL 455 (SC)

From the judgment of the Supreme Court- Act refers to RERA-

"140. It is settled principle of law that if the plain interpretation does not fulfil the mandate and object the Act, this Court has to interpret the law in consonance with the spirit and purpose of the statute. There is indeed a visible inconsistency in the powers of the authority regarding refund of the amount received by the promoter and the provision of law in Section 18 and the text of the provision by which such refund can be referred under Section 40(1). While harmonising the construction of the scheme of the Act with the right of recovery as mandated in Section 40(1) of the Act keeping in mind the intention of the legislature to provide for a speedy recovery if the amount invested by the allottee along with the interest incurred thereon is self-explanatory. However, if Section 40(1) is strictly construed and it is understood to mean that only penalty and interest on the principal amount are recoverable as arrears of land revenue, it would defeat the basic purpose of the Act.

141.Taking into consideration the scheme of the Act what is to be returned to the allottee is his own life savings with interest on computed/quantified by the authority becomes recoverable and such arrear becomes enforceable in law. There appears some ambiguity in section 40(1) of the Act that in our view, by harmonising the provision with the purpose of the Act, is given effect to the provisions is allowed to operate rather running either of them redundant, noticing purport of the legislature and the above-stated principle into consideration we make it clear that the amount which has been determined and refundable to the allottees/home buyers either by the authority or the adjudicating officer in terms of the order is recoverable within the ambit of Section 40(1) of the Act."

20. Works contract service:—

Revised definition of works contract service covers works contracts relating to both movable and immovable property (Till 30-6-2012, these covered only immovable property).

Comprehensive AMC job work using own material (e.g., job of painting car when the job worker uses his own paint), Xeroxing, Photography, etc., can get covered, in addition to construction services. Hence, service tax payable on 70 per cent of value [Till 30-6-2012, there was no specific provision for these services].

In case of finishing services relating to immovable property (like painting, flooring, etc.), service tax payable on 60 per cent of value with effect from 1-7-2012 [Till 30-6-2012, there was no specific provision for these services].

Value of FOC material (like cement, steel, etc., supplied by contractee) was required to be added for composition scheme. To overcome this provision, some service receivers were charging for such supply but at very low price. To get over such tax planning, it has been provided that 'Fair Market Value' of material supplied by contractee should be added.
